The fully automated tool is used to characterize 300mm wafer processes by performing non-destructive measurements on vias, trench widths, depths, sidewall slopes, and linewidths down to 0.18-microns and below. 

The DEKTAK V 300-SL is an advanced stylus-based metrology system which enables monitoring of semiconductor processes on wafers up to 300mm in an automated environment. It delivers the industry's best step height repeatability and highest horizontal resolution, as well as long scan capabilities for 300mm, edge-to-edge scanning. The system conforms closely with the guidelines set forth by the International 300mm Initiative (i300i) consortium based in Austin, Texas, of which Siemens is a member. 

"We are delighted to have been selected by Semiconductor 300 as their partner to provide metrology systems for the world's first integrated 300mm line." said Dr. Timothy Stultz, Vice President and General Manager, Veeco Process Metrology, Santa Barbara. "These orders for the Dektak SXM-320 and Dektak Series V demonstrate Veeco's commitment to provide complete metrology solutions for next generation semiconductor processes."

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--May 4, 1998-- 

Hog Farming Odor-Eater, Microchip Locator, Tissue Regenerator and 

Air Turbulence Reducer Take Top Honors in World's Largest K-12 

Student Science Competition 

The Toshiba/NSTA ExploraVision Awards Program today announced its 12 winning teams for 1998, rewarding students for their visions of future technologies. Among this year's winning student entries are ideas for such innovative scientific advancements as a microchip that helps you locate keys or other small objects instantly; knee replacements that grow once surgically implanted; a new metal alloy designed to reduce airplane turbulence; the "Tooth Buffer," a device that professionally cleans your teeth in 30 seconds; paper made from genetically engineered Duckweed; an artificial heart made from body tissues; and a filtering system that "takes the stink out of hog farming" and converts waste into electric power. (See complete list of winners attached.) 

The 1998 Toshiba/NSTA ExploraVision Awards program chose its 12 top winning teams from a pool of more than 5,000 team entries in the world's largest K-12 student science competition. The four first-place and eight second-place teams, selected from regional winners, will be flown to Washington D.C. for a gala awards weekend June 11-14, at which time they will be awarded their prizes. The awards weekend will feature presentations from science, government and industry notables at a Science Showcase to be held at the Russell Caucus Room on Capitol Hill. David Heil, of the acclaimed TV show "Newton's Apple," will be a special guest for the awards ceremony. 

Gerry Wheeler, Executive Director of the NSTA, commented on this year's ExploraVision winners, noting: "It's obvious that today's students have a real optimism for the future, as well as a desire to learn and build on our society's scientific foundations to make the world a better place." 

Kanichi Ito, Chairman and CEO of Toshiba America, Inc., noted: "We know that the technologies of tomorrow will depend on the active participation of today's students, and based on the creativity and inspiration shown by the ExploraVision students, we're confident that the 21st century will be full of exciting inventions and discoveries." 

Working in teams of 3 or 4 with a teacher-advisor, students use their imaginations to envision a form of technology 20 years from now and compete by sharing their vision through written descriptions and story boards. At a June 12 awards ceremony, members of the four first-place teams will each receive a $10,000 U.S. savings bond (or a Canadian savings bond of comparable issue price); members of the eight second-place teams will each receive $5,000 U.S. or comparable issue price Canadian savings bonds. Schools and teachers of the twelve finalist teams will each receive their choice of selected Toshiba products. 

Deadline to submit entries for the 1999 competition is February 1999. For more information or an application, write to Toshiba/NSTA ExploraVision Awards, National Science Teachers Association, 1840 Wilson Blvd., Arlington, VA. 22201, call 1-800-EXPLOR-9 or (703) 243-7100, or e-mail exploravision@nsta.org. Also see competition information on the World Wide Web http://www.nsta.org/programs/exploravision.html or http://www.toshiba.com/tai/exploravision/index2.html. 

The Toshiba/NSTA ExploraVision Awards program, funded by the Toshiba Corporation, the Toshiba America Group Companies, the Toshiba America Foundation, and administered by the National Science Teachers Association, is open to U.S. and Canadian students. 

The National Science Teachers Association is the largest professional organization in the world committed to improving science education at all levels -- preschool through college. NSTA's current membership includes more than 53,000 science teachers, science supervisors, administrators, business and industry representatives, scientists and others involved in science education. 

The Toshiba Corporation, based in Tokyo, is a world leader in products involving electronics and energy. Toshiba America, Inc. is the holding company for Toshiba's five operating companies with more than 10,000 employees in the United States. The Toshiba America Foundation supports science and mathematics education across the United States.

Veeco Metrology Receives Order From AMD for Multiple Semiconductor Systems 

633 words 
26 May 1998

Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

SANTA BARBARA, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--May 26, 1998-- 

$2M Order To Be Delivered To Fab 30 In Dresden, Germany 

Veeco Metrology recently received an order for multiple metrology systems valued at over $2 million from Advanced Micro Devices (NYSE:AMD). The order includes Critical Dimension Atomic Force Microscopy (CD-AFM) and stylus profilometry systems. Delivery is scheduled for the second quarter of 1998, for installation at AMD's Fab 30 in Dresden, Germany. The systems to be installed include the new DEKTAK SXM-320 automated CD-AFM and the DEKTAK SERIES V automated stylus profilers. These metrology tools incorporate cleanroom engineering with robotic handling and integrated SMIF interface. 

"Veeco's advanced semiconductor metrology tools are critical for monitoring our production process and will assist us in developing our next generation devices," said Mr. Hans Deppe, Operations Director at AMD's Fab 30. "Veeco's ability to provide the highest performance in a broad range of metrology solutions, coupled with their worldwide support infrastructure, were key elements in our decision." 

"This order from AMD demonstrates the growing acceptance in the market of the SXM-320 and the Dektak Series V as next generation, production capable metrology tools," said Dr. Timothy Stultz, Vice President and General Manager, Veeco Metrology, Santa Barbara. "The unique capabilities of the CD-AFM and superior performance of the surface profilers exemplify Veeco's ability to provide state of the art metrology solutions for advanced 0.25 micron geometry wafer fabs." 

The DEKTAK SXM-320 is the only CD-AFM to meet the needs of advanced, semiconductor wafer fabs for in-line topographical and critical dimension metrology solutions. The fully automated tool is used to characterize photolithographic and etch processes by performing non-destructive measurements of linewidths down to 0.18 micron and below, as well as via and trench depth, side wall slope angle, and 3-D micro-topography of surface textures and defects. 

The DEKTAK V 200-SL is an advanced metrology system that enables monitoring of semiconductor processes in an automated environment. High precision, stylus-based measurement technology delivers unsurpassed step height repeatability for monitoring etch and deposition process uniformity, as well as long scan capabilities for measuring CMP planarity or thin film stress on wafers. The linear encoded sample stage with 0.25 micron resolution and a versatile pattern recognition system ensures the industry's best sample positioning repeatability for multi-site measurement recipes. 

Veeco Metrology, with operations in Santa Barbara, California and Tucson, Arizona, is a division of Veeco Instruments Inc. (NASDAQ: VECO). Headquartered in Plainview, New York, Veeco is a worldwide leader in etch and deposition Process Equipment for data storage, Process Metrology tools for the data storage, semiconductor and flat panel display industries. Manufacturing and engineering facilities are located in New York, California and Arizona. Global sales and service offices are located throughout the United States, Europe, Japan and Asia-Pacific.

PLAINVIEW, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--May 29, 1998--At its Annual Meeting today, the shareholders of Veeco Instruments Inc. (NASDAQ:VECO) approved the Company's previously announced merger with Digital Instruments, Inc. of Santa Barbara, CA, a world leader in scanning probe/atomic force microscopy (SPM/AFM). 

Mr. Edward H. Braun, Chairman, President and CEO of Veeco commented, "This merger supports Veeco's strategy to extend our leadership position in metrology by providing customer solutions over a wide range of measurement technologies including atomic force microscopy, optical profilers, stylus profilers, and laser scatterometers. Digital Instruments' products complement our SXM-320 production Atomic Force Microscope, currently built by IBM and sold exclusively by Veeco. As data storage and semiconductor industries continue to shrink device dimensions, scanning atomic force microscopy, now critical for process development and research, will become the next generation production metrology tool for .18 and .13 micron critical dimensions." 

Mr. Braun added, "Digital Instruments ideally fits our acquisition profile: it is a leader in its product area and is synergistic with our core products and markets. This is an excellent example of combining two companies that together can grow faster than they would have individually." 

Under the merger, Digital Instruments shareholders received 5,583,725 shares of Veeco common stock. The merger will be accounted for as a pooling of interests transaction. Digital Instruments, which was privately held, had revenues of approximately $51 million in 1997. 

Also at today's meeting, Veeco's shareholders appointed five new members to the Company's Board of Directors, including three new outside directors and two executives from Digital Instruments, and reappointed two individuals already serving on the Company's Board. This brings the Company's total board membership to 11. The five newly elected directors are: Roger D. McDaniel, Irwin H. Pfister, Heinz K. Fridrich, Virgil Elings and John Gurley. Mr. McDaniel is President, CEO and a director of Integrated Process Equipment Corp. (NASDAQ: IPEC), a leading manufacturer of CMP (chemical-mechanical planarization) equipment for the semiconductor industry. Mr. Pfister is Executive Vice President and corporate officer of Schlumberger Ltd. Mr. Fridrich serves as a professor, Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering, University of Florida, and was formerly Vice President and General Manager of IBM's largest development and manufacturing site for semiconductor and electronic packaging. Mr. Elings and Mr. Gurley are co-founders and President and Vice President of Digital, respectively. Mr. James C. Wyant and Mr. Walter J. Scherr were reelected to Veeco's Board of Directors. 

Veeco Instruments Inc., headquartered in Plainview, New York, is a worldwide leader in etch and deposition Process Equipment for data storage, and Metrology tools for the data storage, semiconductor and flat panel display industries. Manufacturing and engineering facilities are located in New York, California and Arizona. Global sales and service offices are located throughout the United States, Europe, Japan and Asia-Pacific.

Veeco Receives New $2.1 Million Order for Automated Atomic Force Microscopes; For Advanced MR Head Production

Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

PLAINVIEW, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--June 3, 1998--Veeco Instruments Inc. (NASDAQ:VECO), today announced it has received a new $2.1 million order for three Dimension(TM) 9000 Atomic Force Microscopes (AFMs) from a leading U.S. data storage manufacturer. The systems will be used to measure wafer-level step height on advanced magnetoresistive (MR) thin film magnetic heads (TFMHs) during production. Shipments are expected to be completed by the end of the year. 

This order follows a previous order for the Dimension 9000 from a major thin film head manufacturer that will ship by the end of this quarter to a Japanese site. 

"We are pleased that two leading data storage manufacturers have chosen our new AFM tools for their next generation MR head production, which indicates customer acceptance of this new, fully automatic AFM. The $2.1 M order is also the single largest order received to date by Digital Instruments," David S. Perloff, President of Veeco Metrology, commented. 

The orders are for Digital Instruments' Dimension 9000 AFM, which is capable of measuring features as small as 2nm, as well as sub-nanometer vertical features, with excellent repeatability. The system provides cassette-to-cassette wafer handling, automatic tip characterization, automatic tip replacement, and pattern recognition/vision for fully automated operation. Data storage applications include measuring step height, roughness and other parameters on TFMHs and wafers. 

On May 29, Veeco announced it had merged with Digital Instruments, Inc. of Santa Barbara, CA, a world leader in scanning probe/atomic force microscopy (SPM/AFM).

WHITE PLAINS, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--June 5, 1998--A class action suit (98 Civ. 3450)(Coar, J.) was filed yesterday in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois (Eastern Division) on behalf of purchasers of the common stock of Nanophase Technologies Corporation ("Nanophase") during the period November 26, 1997 through and including January 8, 1998 (the "Class Period"). 

The Complaint charges Nanophase and certain of its officers and directors with violations of the federal securities laws by making materially false and misleading statements about Nanophase's sales and earnings in connection with the initial public offering of Nanophase's common stock. 

As alleged in the Complaint, due to the issuance of false and misleading statements concerning Nanophase's business and true financial condition, the price of Nanophase's common stock was artificially inflated during the Class Period and caused plaintiffs to pay more than they should have for Nanophase's common stock or to buy the stock when, had the true facts been disclosed, they would not have done so at all. 

Plaintiffs seek to recover damages on behalf of all purchasers of Nanophase common stock during the Class Period. Plaintiffs are represented by the law firms of Lowey Dannenberg Bemporad & Selinger, P.C. and Susman & Watkins, firms with extensive experience prosecuting class and securities fraud actions on behalf of shareholders. 

Any member of the proposed class may move the Court to serve as lead plaintiff on or before August 3, 1998. In order to serve as lead plaintiff, however, you must meet certain legal requirements.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--June 8, 1998--A putative class action has been filed in the United States District Court for the Central District of Illinois on behalf of a class of purchasers of Nanophase Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ: NANX) common stock on or traceable to the company's initial public offering of 4,000,000 shares, from Nov. 26, 1997, through Jan. 8, 1998, inclusive (the "Class Period").

Five New Members Named to Elite WITI Women in Science and Technology Hall of Fame; Outstanding Women to be Honored June 25 at Women in Technology International, WITI, 1998 Technology Summit 

1,407 words 
9 June 1998
13:27 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--June 9, 1998--Five women who have made their mark in science and technology -- from a Nobel Prize-winner who co-developed two of the first successful leukemia treatment drugs as well as acyclovir, the first selective antiviral against the herpes infection virus (HIV), to the principal investigator of an asteroid and comet discovery program run by the prestigious Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) -- have been chosen by an independent panel of judges to the Women in Science and Technology (WITI) Hall of Fame. 

The premiere award for women in science and technology worldwide, the WITI Hall of Fame was launched in 1996 to recognize, honor, and promote the outstanding contributions women make to the scientific and technological communities and society at large. This year's five inductees are Dr. Anita Borg, Dr. Mildred S. Dresselhaus, Gertrude B. Elion, Julie Spicer England, and Dr. Eleanor Francis Helin. 

The new WITI Hall of Fame inductees will be honored at ceremonies on Thursday, June 25, at 7 p.m., during the WITI 1998 Technology Summit in Santa Clara, Calif. The largest-ever conference of top women in technology, the WITI 1998 Technology Summit will draw more than 3,500 technologists and scientists from around the world. 

Featured speakers at the event include Esther Dyson, president of EDventure Holdings and author of "Release 2.0: A Design for Living in the Digital Age;" Kim Polese, CEO, Marimba, Inc.; Donna Shirley, manager, Mars Exploration Program, Jet Propulsion Laboratory, and other notables. Members of the WITI Hall of Fame are also publicly recognized on WITI's award-winning Web site. 

"WITI is committed to recognizing the accomplishments of outstanding women who often remain anonymous to the outside world, and the WITI Hall of Fame is a demonstration of that commitment," says Carolyn Leighton, founder and executive director of WITI. "We're honored to pay tribute to the significant contributions of Dr. Anita Borg, Dr. Mildred S. Dresselhaus, Gertrude B. Elion, Julie Spicer England, and Eleanor Francis Helin, and include them in the WITI Hall of Fame." 

The prestigious independent panel of judges included: Laura DiDio, senior editor, Computerworld; Alan Hall, contributing editor, Scientific American; Patty Lund, CEO, Upstart Communications; Sandy Reed, editor-in-chief, InfoWorld. 


Inductee Profiles


Dr. Anita Borg is a computer scientist in the Office of the Chief Technologist at Xerox Corp.'s Palo Alto Research Center (PARC). At the Digital Equipment Corp. (DEC) Western Research Laboratory in the 1980s, Dr. Borg developed and patented a method for generating complete address traces used for designing and analyzing high-speed computer memory systems. 

In 1987, Dr. Borg founded "systers", a 2500 member international virtual community for technical women in computing. In 1994, she founded the Grace Hopper Celebration of Women in Computing, the first technical conference for women in computing. Today, Dr. Borg is supported by Xerox in her effort to create the Institute for Women in Technology, an experimental R&D organization focusing on increasing the impact of women on technology and expanding the positive impact of technology on the world's women. 

Currently the chair of the board of the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) and an Institute Professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Dr. Mildred Dresselhaus has received numerous awards, including the National Medal of Science and 13 honorary doctorates. 

Dr. Dresselhaus is the co-author of three books on carbon science, and her research has focused on experimental solid-state physics, particularly in carbon-related materials and their intercalation compounds. Fullerenes and fullerene-related carbon nanotubes are Dr. Dresselhaus' most recent areas of interest and research. 

A recipient of the 1988 Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine, Gertrude B. Elion is scientist emeritus with Glaxo Wellcome, Inc. Elion is credited with the synthesis and co-development of two of the first successful drugs for the treatment of leukemia, as well as azathioprine, an agent to prevent the rejection of kidney transplants and to treat rheumatoid arthritis. Elion also played a major role in the development of allopurinol for the treatment of gout, and of acyclovir, the first selective antiviral against herpes virus infections. 

Julie Spicer England is vice president, Texas Instruments (TI), and a business manager in the Worldwide Application Specific Products business unit in TI's largest division, the Semiconductor Group. In this role, England manages a $300 million business which includes the custom Reduced Instruction Set Computing microprocessor product line using leading-edge technology and a start-up business based on digital signal processor printer applications. A senior member technical staff emeritus at TI, England is the co-inventor of six patents related to infrared process technology. 

Dr. Eleanor F. Helin has been active in planetary science and astronomy for almost three decades years at the California Institute of Technology and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL). In the early 1970s, Helin initiated the Palomar Planet-Crossing Asteroid Survey (PCAS) from Palomar Observatory, and that program has been responsible for the discovery of thousands of asteroids of all types including one hundred near-earth asteroids. One of the most significant discoveries was that of asteroid (2026) Aten, the first asteroid found to have an orbit smaller than the Earth. In 1995, after conducting the PCAS photographic search program for nearly 25 years, Helin began to concentrate on bringing online a new, upgraded search program using electronic sensors and a large aperture telescope. Helin is principal investigator for the Near Earth Asteroid Tracking Program (NEAT), which has already discovered a significant number of near-earth objects as the program moves into its third year of operation. The NEAT program is a NASA-JPL/Airforce collaboration. 

The sponsors of the WITI Women in Science and Technology Hall of Fame are American Airlines; Cadillac Motor Car Division; Charles Schwab & Co., Inc.; Computer Associates International Inc.; CMP Media; Dell Computer Corp.; Digital Equipment Corp.; Ernst & Young; IBM Corp.; and Working Woman Magazine. WITI Hall of Fame inductees are chosen by an independent panel of judges. 

Previous inductees have included the world's first six computer programmers; and Donna Shirley, JPL's manager for the Mars Exploration Program. 

To register for the 1998 WITI Technology Summit and attend the Hall of Fame event on June 25, visit the WITI Web site at www.witi.org or call WITI at 800/334-9484. 


About WITI


Women in Technology International (WITI), founded in 1989 by Carolyn Leighton, executive director, is a rapidly growing worldwide association of over 6,000 (and an active database of over 25,000) professional women and men working in science and technology organizations. WITI is dedicated to creating new possibilities for women to advance and succeed in technology. 

WITI's mission is to advance women to executive-level positions, to help women become more technologically literate and financially independent, and to motivate young women to choose careers in science and technology. WITI sponsors include: Exclusive: AMD; American Airlines; Autodesk; Bay Networks; Bernard Hodes Advertising; Cadillac Motor Car Division; Charles Schwab & Co., Inc.; Check Point Software Technologies, Inc.; Cisco Systems; Computer Associates International, Inc.; Dell Computer Corp.; Deloitte Consulting and Deloitte & Touche LLP; Digital Equipment Corp.; Electronics for Imaging; Ernst & Young LLP; IBM; Intel Corp.; Kauffman Center for Entrepreneurial Leadership; Microsoft Corp.; PeopleSoft; Price Waterhouse; Quantum Corp.; Raytheon Co.; RHI Consulting; Sun Microsystems; Sunday Examiner & Chronicle's CAREER SEARCH; Texas Instruments; Universal Studios; UpStart Communications; Working Woman Magazine; and Xerox Corp. Gold: Allied Signal; Amdahl; Apple Computer; Business Wire; Compaq; CrossWorlds Software, Inc.; EDS; Hitachi Data Systems; InfoWorld; Intuit; Mentor Graphics Corp.; Morgan Stanley Dean Witter; Mosaix, Inc.; Motorola; N.E.T.; Rockwell Semiconductor Systems; Seagate Technology; Sony Electronics, Inc.; VLSI Technology; and Xilinx. Silver: Adaptec, Inc.; Applied Materials; KPMG Peat Marwick; Levi Strauss & Co.; LifeScan, Inc.; Netscape Communications; Oracle Corp.; and Qualcomm. Supporting Patrons: 3Com; Jones, Day, Reavis & Pogue; Silicon Valley Bank; Solectron Corp.; and Systems Partners.

Etec Awarded DARPA Contract for Advanced Microcolumn Research 

534 words 
7 July 1998
20:27 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

HAYWARD, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--July 7, 1998--Etec Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:ETEC), a leader in patterning solutions for the worldwide electronics industries, today announced that it has been awarded a four year contract to develop advanced multiple electron beam microcolumns for nanolithography. 

The award, from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) and the Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), will amount to approximately $4 million. 

"We are pleased to continue our relationship with these agencies," stated Steve Cooper, Etec's chairman, president and CEO. "Working in conjunction with DARPA/NAVAIR, Etec will be able to support future government microelectronics needs as well as continue research and development efforts for future Etec products. This award complements an earlier (July, 1997), $6.8 million multi-source award and will contribute significantly to our microcolumn program and to our success in the future." 

Microcolumns are miniaturized electron beam columns dramatically smaller than conventional columns. Configured in close arrays, it is believed they will provide high patterning throughput and high performance and bring a revolutionary departure from today's lithography techniques. 

The work to be performed at Etec will support DARPA's nanolithography project initiatives, which are aimed at building core technologies to meet future military microelectronics needs.

These risks and uncertainties include risks associated with the timely development and market acceptance of new products, entry into a new market, availability of key components, developing full manufacturing capability from prototype construction on a cost-effective basis, delays in factory testing and acceptance, quality control problems and the development of competitive products or processes. Statements in this release are based upon internal estimates, preliminary information and management assumptions which are subject to a number of risks and uncertainties inherent in estimating future results. Other risks detailed from time to time in the Company's SEC reports including the annual report filed on Form 10-K and subsequent filings on Form 10-Q. The Company assumes no obligation to update the information in this release. 

About Etec: Etec Systems, Inc. is a leader in patterning solutions for the worldwide semiconductor and electronics industries. Its products include electron-and laser-beam systems that produce high-precision masks, which are used to print circuit patterns onto semiconductor wafers and high-speed, large-area laser direct imaging systems and e-beam test equipment for electronic interconnect and flat panel display production applications. Founded in 1970, the company is headquartered in Hayward, Calif., with manufacturing facilities in Hayward, Calif., Beaverton, Ore., Tucson, Ariz., and Feldkirchen, Germany, with sales and service offices worldwide. Etec's stock is traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the symbol ETEC. The Company's World Wide Web site can be accessed at www.etec.com.

Cascade Microtech and Micron Force Instruments to Jointly Develop a New Generation of IC Probing Product 

522 words 
13 July 1998
12:18 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--July 13, 1998--Cascade Microtech Inc. and Micron Force Instruments (MFI) announced today a cooperative agreement to jointly develop a new generation of IC probing technology. 

The new technology will be aimed at the semiconductor failure analysis and yield management markets and will address the challenges that shrinking process geometries pose to physical design and failure analysis of complex ICs. 

The initial product from the joint efforts will be a contact probe/positioner for use on a new wafer probe station, optimized for sub-micron probing. Products will also be available to extend the capabilities of Cascade's highly successful Alessi and Summit analytical probe stations. To achieve the required performance the probe station will use an innovative Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) approach pioneered by MFI. This approach allows nanometer imaging of IC features and the precise control of probes. 

David Fisher, president and CEO of MFI, commented, "We are very pleased to have the opportunity to work with Cascade Microtech, the world leader in on-wafer characterization. As IC features shrink below .25 micron, optical positioning of probes becomes problematic. Our joint efforts will allow the introduction of new probing solutions to match the needs created by process shrinks below .25 micron." 

By extending the limits of internal node probing, the new probe station addresses key concerns outlined in the SIA semiconductor technology roadmap, an industry publication which forecasts semiconductor technology trends and challenges. 

"Throughout our history Cascade has been a technology leader. We view our investment in MFI as a continuation of our commitment to successfully bring unique and essential new probing technologies to market," stated Eric Strid, CEO of Cascade Microtech. "The combination of our probe and measurement expertise with MFI's AFM based positioning capability will provide an enabling solution for our customer's next generation analytical probing requirements." 

Based in Beaverton, Ore., Cascade Microtech Inc. is the world leader in advanced microelectronic probing solutions. Cascade manufactures a comprehensive line of probe stations, probe cards, accessories and software, used to characterize semiconductor devices on wafer. Cascade's web site is www.cmicro.com. For more information, please contact David Quane, Product Marketing Manager at 503/643-7779 or davidq@cmicro.com. 

Micron Force Instruments Inc. (MFI), based in San Jose, Calif., is a venture start-up based on the commercialization of unique internal node IC probing technologies. 

In addition to the nano-positioning capability of the joint MFI/Cascade Microtech product, MFI will introduce a line of non-contact Electro Force Sampling (EFS) probes that provide sub-micron positioning and high speed waveform capture with negligible loading to the DUT (device under test). For more information, please contact Rich Wiley, V.P. Marketing at 408/501-0793 or richw@micronforce.com. 

CONTACT: Cascade Microtech David Quane, 503/643-7779 davidq@cmicro.com. or Micron Force Instruments Rich Wiley, 408/501-0793 richw@micronforce.com. or Kirkpatrick Communications Bruce Kirkpatrick, 510/651-9229 brucekirk@kirk-com.com. 08:03 EDT JULY 13, 1998

Ben-Abraham Technologies Completes Audited Financials; Files With Alberta Stock Exchange 

898 words 
27 July 1998
15:01 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

LINCOLNSHIRE, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--July 27, 1998--Ben-Abraham Technologies Inc. (ASE:BAI) ("B A Tech") a U.S. biopharmaceutical company, today announced it has received an unqualified opinion on its 1997 financial statements. 

The audit was conducted in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). These financial statements and the report of the auditors have been filed with the Alberta Stock Exchange and trading in B A Tech stock is expected to resume shortly. The company's auditors are Deloitte & Touche. 

Stephen M. Simes, vice-chairman, president and CEO, said, "We are pleased to be able to file our audited financial statements for 1997. The temporary trading suspension on our stock allowed us time to finalize the financial statements, complete the audit and disseminate the information to our shareholders. We are committed to timely filing of our financial statements and communications with our shareholders now and in the future." 

For the year ended Dec. 31, 1997, the net loss decreased to $1.9 million from a net loss of $6.2 million for the period from August 29, 1996 (date of incorporation) to Dec. 31, 1996. The net loss per share for the year-end 1997 was five cents per share compared with the 1996 short-period net loss per share of 26 cents per share. 

Also filed with the audited 1997 financial statements are the first quarter 1998 unaudited financial statements. For the first quarter ended March 31, 1998, the net loss was $579,000, or two cents per share, compared with a loss of $404,000, or one cent per share, for the prior years three months. Second quarter financial statements will be completed and filed on time in August. 

"A number of key events have occurred since the end of 1997 that are critical for the future of the company," Simes said. Among the most important are the following: 


1)   Louis W. Sullivan, M.D. has become chairman of the board.
2)   Angela Ho of New York City, originally from Hong Kong and Macao,
     joined the company's board.
3)   Phillip B. Donenberg, CPA, has joined our company as chief
     financial officer and treasurer.
4)   All Class A shares previously owned by Avi Ben-Abraham M.D.,
     former chairman and CEO, have been converted into subordinate
     voting shares, with the company receiving a $3.75 million
     payment.
5)   Approximately 1.4 million Class A shares were returned to the
     company's treasury by Ben-Abraham.
6)   Two investors in Hong Kong converted 2 million Class A shares to
     subordinate voting shares through a $500,000 payment to the
     company.
7)   Our laboratory in Smyrna, Ga. is fully operational, allowing us
     to accelerate product development.


"We believe these advances will help B A Tech reach its long term goal of increasing shareholder value by building a successful pharmaceutical company", said Simes. 

Current Shares Outstanding 

Of the original 20 million Class A shares issued and outstanding at December 1996, only approximately 1.5 million remain outstanding after conversions to date: 17 million have been converted to subordinate voting shares, and about 1.5 million Class A shares have been returned to the company's treasury. 

Currently there are approximately 1.5 million Class A shares, 3.3 million Class C shares and 29.4 million subordinate voting shares outstanding. Of these, about 14 million subordinate voting shares are in an escrow agreement and subject to a "lock up" preventing sale for 13 months except under certain conditions. In summary, there are approximately 34.3 million shares currently outstanding. As of June 30, 1998, the company's cash balance is about $3.75 million. 

B A Tech is a biopharmaceutical company. It is developing and commercializing a proprietary nanoparticle technology for novel vaccines, drug delivery systems, cancer therapies and targeted therapeutics. The company will grow through developing its core technology and by in-licensing additional late-stage pharmaceutical products to expand its product portfolio. 

Certain statements in this news release may constitute forward looking statements which are not historical facts, and involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ from those expected and projected.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--July 29, 1998--Harris & Harris Group, Inc. (Nasdaq/NMS:HHGP) announced today that its net asset value per share (NAV) at June 30, 1998 was $2.16. The decline in NAV in the quarter and six months ended June 30, 1998 also reflected significant declines in the market values of the Company's holdings in the stocks of three publicly traded companies: Nanophase Technologies Corporation, Princeton Video Image, Inc. and Voice Control Systems, Inc. 

Harris & Harris Group had originally invested in Nanophase and Princeton Video as private equity investments before their respective initial public offerings in late 1997. On June 30, 1998, Harris & Harris Group owned 730,916 shares of Nanophase, 150,200 shares of Princeton Video and 268,343 shares of Voice Control Systems. 

Harris & Harris Group is a Business Development Company with 10,641,400 common shares issued and outstanding, net of a total of 61,400 shares that the Company has repurchased in the open market in 1998 at an average price of $2.70 per share.

Veeco Reports Results for the Second Quarter and First Six Months of 1998 

1,544 words 
29 July 1998
21:32 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

PLAINVIEW, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--July 29, 1998--Veeco Instruments Inc. (NASDAQ: VECO), today reported financial results for the second quarter and six months ended June 30, 1998. The Company's results were in line with its expectations announced in a press release on July 7, 1998. Historical financial results have been restated to reflect the merger of Veeco and Digital Instruments, which closed on May 29, 1998, using the pooling of interests accounting method. 


Second Quarter Results


Sales for the second quarter of 1998 decreased 6% to $51.1 million from $54.5 million for the second quarter of 1997. Veeco's Metrology product sales increased 30% over the prior year, reflecting the increased use of the Company's products for in-line inspection of critical production steps in data storage applications. Veeco's Process Equipment product sales decreased 48% from the prior year's second quarter, as sales of ion beam etch products declined, while sales of new ion beam deposition equipment increased for use in high density thin film magnetic head (TFMH) data storage applications. Ion beam etch sales continue to be negatively effected by excess industry capacity in data storage. 

Operating income, exclusive of a non-recurring $7.5 million pre-tax charge for merger and reorganization costs principally related to the merger with Digital Instruments, decreased to $5.9 million in the second quarter of 1998 from $11.3 million, excluding a $4.2 million in-process R&D charge from the acquisition of certain assets of the Materials Research Corporation, in the second quarter of 1997. The $7.5 million charge is comprised of transaction costs of $3.3 million, $1.6 million non-cash compensation charge related to stock issued in accordance with a pre-existing agreement with a key Digital Instruments' employee, $1.4 million of duplicate facilities costs and $1.2 million of reorganization costs. Including the merger expense and reorganization charge, Veeco reported a net loss of $1.8 million for the second quarter of 1998, compared with net income of $5.7 million for the second quarter of last year, including the in-process R&D charge. Operating profits in 1998 were impacted by higher operating expenses compared to 1997. The Company continues to invest in research and development for both its Metrology and Process Equipment businesses in order to ensure the flow of new products to these key segments. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased as Veeco expanded its sales efforts, applications support and worldwide service. Pro forma diluted earnings per share on a fully taxed basis was $0.24 for the second quarter of 1998, excluding the merger and reorganization expenses, compared with $0.46 per share for the corresponding period of 1997, on a fully taxed basis excluding the in-process R&D charge. Including the charge, Veeco reported a loss of $0.12 per share for the second quarter of 1998. 

Bookings for the second quarter of 1998 were $50.0 million, a 16% decrease from the prior year second quarter. Second quarter 1998 Metrology orders increased 24% from the prior year, while Process Equipment orders were off sharply, showing a 52% decline from the second quarter of 1997. Veeco's book/bill ratio for the second quarter of 1998 was .98 to 1. 


First Half Results


Sales for the six-month period ended June 30, 1998 increased 1% to $104.8 million from $103.8 million for the first six months of 1997. Veeco's Metrology product sales increased 27% over the prior year, while Veeco's Process Equipment product sales decreased 34% from the prior year's first half. 

Operating income, excluding the merger and reorganization charge, decreased to $13.6 million in the first half of 1998 from $21.2 million in the first half of 1997, excluding the in-process R&D charge. Including the merger and reorganization expense, Veeco reported net income of $3.9 million for the first half of 1998, compared with net income of $13.0 million in the first six months of last year, including the in-process R&D charge. Operating profits in the first six months of 1998 were impacted by higher operating expenses compared to 1997, due to increased investment in research and development, as well as expanded sales efforts, applications support and worldwide service. Pro forma diluted earnings per share on a fully taxed basis was $0.56 for the first six months of 1998, excluding the merger and reorganization expense, versus $0.88 per share for the corresponding period of 1997, on a fully taxed basis excluding the in-process R&D charge. Including the charge, Veeco reported first-half 1998 earnings per share of $0.27. 

Bookings for the first six months of 1998 were $115.9 million, a 7% increase from the prior year's first half bookings of $108.1 million. First half 1998 Metrology orders increased 42% from the prior year, while Process Equipment orders decreased 24%. Veeco's book/bill ratio for the first half of 1998 was 1.10 to 1. 

Edward H. Braun, Chairman, President and CEO of Veeco commented, "Weak data storage and semiconductor market conditions, accompanied by industry-wide over-capacity, end of quarter rescheduling of customer deliveries and falling hard drive prices, continue to impact Veeco's performance. The Company continues to take appropriate spending and head count reduction actions. Veeco's six month book-to-bill ratio was 1.10 to 1, and at the current time we expect calendar 1998 revenue to be flat with restated 1997 revenues of $217 million." 

"Although business conditions remain difficult industry-wide, we are encouraged by the strength of our metrology business, which accounted for 67% of second quarter sales, and the performance of our new ion beam deposition business," added Mr. Braun. "Veeco shipped a record $34.4 million of Metrology products during the second quarter, including significant growth of in-line optical metrology and atomic force microscopy products for critical data storage applications." 

"As the technology transition in data storage progresses and our customers' business fundamentals improve, we will be well positioned for an upturn," added Mr. Braun. "Veeco expects to benefit from the data storage conversion to magnetoresistive (MR) and giant magnetoresistive (GMR) technology, the increased use of in-line metrology and the shift to smaller thin film magnetic heads. We continue to believe that Veeco's acquisition strategy to broaden our technology and product offerings, most recently with the Metrology product additions of Digital Instruments and Wyko, supports the Company's long-term growth outlook." 

Veeco Instruments Inc., headquartered in Plainview, New York, is a worldwide leader in Metrology tools for the data storage and semiconductor industries, and etch and deposition Process Equipment for the data storage industry. Manufacturing and engineering facilities are located in New York, California and Arizona. Global sales and service offices are located throughout the United States, Europe, Japan and Asia-Pacific.

LINCOLNSHIRE, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 5, 1998-- 

Trading Resumption Awaits Alberta Stock Exchange Review 

Ben-Abraham Technologies Inc. ("BA Tech" (Alberta Stock Exchange: BAI)) a U.S. biopharmaceutical company, today announced that each of the three securities commissions to whom B A Tech reports have lifted their cease trading orders. 

These actions resulted from B A Tech's filing 1997 audited financial statements and First Quarter 1998 unaudited financial statements with the commissions on July 24, 1998. 

Trading in B A Tech will resume on the Alberta Stock Exchange once the Exchange lifts its trading suspension. The financial statements also were filed with the Alberta Stock Exchange on July 24. The company received a letter from the Alberta Stock Exchange on July 31 requesting additional information for its customary reinstatement review. 

Stephen M. Simes, president and chief executive officer of B A Tech said, "We are pleased that the Ontario, Alberta and British Columbia Securities Commissions have lifted their temporary cease trading orders and look forward to seeing the Alberta Stock Exchange lift their suspension. We expect to provide the Exchange with the requested information this week. Throughout this process, and in the future, we will continue to keep our shareholders and the investing public informed about B A Tech matters." 

B A Tech is a biopharmaceutical company. It is developing and commercializing a proprietary nanoparticle technology for novel vaccines, vaccine adjuvants and drug delivery systems. The company will grow through developing its core technology and by in-licensing additional late-stage pharmaceutical products to expand its product portfolio.

Orthovita Forms New Subsidiary PARTISYN CORP; Develops Nano-structured Particles 

417 words 
10 August 1998
13:41 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

MALVERN, Pa.--(BW HealthWire)--Aug. 10, 1998--Orthovita Inc. (EASDAQ:VITA), a biomaterials company that develops bone substitutes, announced today that it has formed PARTISYN CORP(TM), a wholly owned subsidiary company that has developed a fine particle synthesis or nano-structured technology. "This exciting technology emanated from the development of our calcium-phosphate bone cement, VITAGRAFT(TM). By forming Partisyn as a wholly owned subsidiary, we plan to exploit the industrial and commercial applications of this technology through licensing and royalty arrangements for this novel process while maintaining our major focus in the development and commercialization of our core business of biomaterials based bone substitutes," according to David S. Joseph, President and Chief Executive Officer. 

Particles or nanomaterials in the nanometer size are infinitely tiny (approximately one-ten thousandth the diameter of a human hair, or one million particles would fit on the head of a pin). In 1995, the Battelle National Laboratory listed what it considered to be the top ten strategic technologies of the future, and that included nanomaterials as one of the "super materials." "Nanomaterials will enhance the performance of basic raw materials used in electronics, paints and pigments, medicine, coatings, cosmetics, chemical polishing of semiconductors, industrial catalysts and structural ceramics and are among just a few examples of the potential applications," stated Orthovita's research scientists. 

Mr. Joseph stated that "Our objective is to license out our novel process that produces nanomaterials to companies in the chemical industry. We hope to have multiple licensing opportunities to cover the broad range of potential applications we believe may ensue over time." 

Orthovita develops, manufactures and markets one of the broadest platform of bone substitutes including BIOGRAN(R), its first commercialized product that is a resorbable, granular biomaterial that biologically transforms to bone; ORTHOCOMP(TM), in development as a composite, high-strength resin cement with a biological interface that bonds to bone that is fast setting and injectable; and VITAGRAFT(TM), in development as an injectable resorbable cement that aids in fracture healing. 

All statements contained in this press release are forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. The Company's documents filed with the U.S. Securities Exchange Commission and the Belgian Banking and Finance Commission identify important factors that might cause actual results to differ materially from those indicated by the forward-looking statements.

Ben-Abraham Technologies Provides Scientific and Financial Update -- Second Quarter Financials Filed

Business Wire

(c) 1998 Business Wire

LINCOLNSHIRE, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sept. 1, 1998--Ben-Abraham Technologies Inc. ["B A Tech" (ASE:BAI)] a U.S. biopharmaceutical company, today announced an update of its research and development and financial position. 

The company's core technology continues to be its nanoparticle technology licensed from the University of California in 1997. This technology currently is protected by nine issued U.S. patents and the subject of patent applications around the world. With the company's laboratory becoming fully operational in January 1998, the company has been able to make continued progress and is in good standing with respect to the Exclusive License Agreement with the University of California. 

The company has completed all milestones required to date under the License Agreement. Based on continuing review and evaluation of product development and the best use of company resources, B A Tech may choose to renegotiate with the University of California to increase emphasis on some projects and decrease emphasis on other projects. 

B A Tech will continue the development of its core technology for various uses including the potential for improved vaccines and drug delivery. The company's objective is to file an IND application for a Phase I Clinical Trial of its nanoparticles as soon as possible. Pending continued progress, the company targets early 1999 for such a filing. The company is manufacturing its current needs of nanoparticles in its GLP (Good Laboratory Practices) laboratory and will determine whether to build, lease, or obtain by other means a GMP (Good Manufacturing Practices) facility for production of larger quantities. 

In addition to working on its core technology, B A Tech is actively seeking to in-license additional pharmaceutical products. The company's objective is to identify and in-license late stage development products. Late stage development products are defined as those that are in or ready for human clinical trials, so as to decrease the level of risk associated with product development. 

In another development, on Aug. 20, 1998, the company filed its second quarter 1998 interim financial statements. These statements reflect a cash balance at June 30, 1998 in excess of $3.9 million compared with $1.8 million as of December 31, 1997. In addition, current liabilities decreased almost $1 million for the same 6-month period ended June 30, 1998. All references to dollars are in U.S. dollars. 

The company's net loss increased by $400,000 and $576,000 for the three and six month periods ended June 30, 1998, respectively, compared to those same periods in 1997 as the company's Smyrna, Georgia laboratory facility became fully operational, allowing the company to accelerate product development. 

B A Tech is a biopharmaceutical company. It is developing and commercializing a proprietary nanoparticle technology for novel vaccines, vaccine adjuvants, and drug delivery systems. The company will grow through developing its core technology and by in-licensing additional late stage pharmaceutical products to expand its product portfolio.

Zygo and IBM Sign Worldwide Distribution Agreement for IBM Atomic Force Microscope

499 words 
12 October 1998
22:21 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

MIDDLEFIELD, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 12, 1998--Zygo Corporation (NASDAQ:ZIGO) today announced it has signed an exclusive worldwide distribution agreement with the IBM Manufacturing Technology Center in Boca Raton, Florida. 

The agreement provides for Zygo to market and sell IBM's most recently developed Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) in all markets world wide under the Zygo label. The system is based on Scanning Tunneling Microscopy technology invented by IBM and recognized by a Nobel Prize in 1986. The system is a multimode scanning probe microscope designed for the measurement of submicron features to angstrom level resolution for the most challenging semiconductor, data storage, and other high technology applications. The benchtop microscope is intended for process development, failure analysis, and yield improvement applications. 

The addition of AFM technology to Zygo's existing automation and metrology capability - interferometric microscopes, interferometric large aperture systems, confocal microscopes, machine vision, and interferometric micropositioning - creates the most comprehensive high precision yield improvement systems capability available to the high technology industries. 

Commenting on the agreement with IBM, Gary K. Willis, president and chief executive officer, stated, "This agreement supports Zygo's strategy to extend our leadership position in yield enhancement by providing customer solutions over a wide range of measurement technologies. As data storage and semiconductor device dimensions continue to shrink, scanning probe microscopes will be critical for process development, research, and production control. The current market for SPMs is over $100 million per year and is expected to more than double over the next five years." Commenting on the agreement, D. E. (Mike) Davis, director of IBM's Manufacturing Technology Center, said, "We are quite pleased to begin a strategic relationship with Zygo. We believe working together has the potential to result in numerous production yield improvement solutions, combining our two organizations' capabilities." 

Zygo Corporation designs, develops, manufactures, and markets high performance measurement and yield improvement instruments, systems, and accessories used in high technology industries. The Company is headquartered in Middlefield, Connecticut, and also has operations in Asslar, Germany; Longmont, Colorado; and in Newbury Park and Sunnyvale, California. Zygo is traded on the Nasdaq National Market under the symbol ZIGO. Additional information on the Company is available on the Internet at www.zygo.com.

Technology Review Takes First Critical Look at World Wide Web Consortium 

694 words 
13 October 1998
14:16 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

CAMBRIDGE, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 13, 1998-- 

Special Issue on "The Unknown Internet" Reports on 

Global Tracking of Potential Epidemics 

In the upcoming special issue on "The Unknown Internet" (Nov./Dec.) of Technology Review, MIT's Magazine of Innovation, the lead story takes the first critical look at the World Wide Web Consortium, or the W3C and its founder, Tim Berners-Lee. TR reports on "little-known" or "little-understood" aspects of how the Internet works, and how it's run and what effect it has on individual lives. 

"TR offers the first look behind the closed doors of what some have called the Web's secret government. Cyber-writer Simson Garfinkel's investigative report shines a light on this organization, which will have a large impact on the Web's structure in the 21st century. To some of the W3C's critics, it is unsettling to think of a consortium made up primarily of corporations, with meetings closed to the outside world, making policy that affects us all," said John Benditt, editor-in-chief, Technology Review. 

Based at MIT, the shadowy W3C has more than 250 corporate members -- companies that have financial stakes in the Internet -- including such giants as Microsoft, Sun Microsystems, IBM and Cisco Systems. The consortium also has as members non-profit organizations, industry groups and government agencies around the world. Its members have a decisive authority on how the Web will operate in the future. In spite of that influence, almost nobody outside the telecommunications industry understands what the W3C is and how it works. 

While its technical work is widely admired, the W3C has raised eyebrows with projects that have more to do with regulating online society than managing the flow of bits. In addition, some in the industry complain that the group's decisions reflect the thinking of one man: Tim Berners-Lee, so-called king of the Web. The top-down, personalized management of the consortium as structured by Berners-Lee, is criticized. 


Web Monitoring of Emerging Diseases


The W3C story is followed up by three reports on unknown aspects of the Net: Web tracking of emerging diseases, bandwidth as a tradable commodity and a real company's transformation to a virtual retail shop. 

- ProMED-Mail, - (www.healthnet.org), "the CNN of epidemiology outbreaks," enables epidemiologists to use the Web to keep pace with emerging viruses anywhere in the world. In the four years since it went online, ProMED-Mail has grown from 40 subscribers in seven countries to 15,000 in 150 countries. It is considered by health experts to be an indispensable medium for tracking the global spread of ebola, AIDS, and other infectious diseases, and for transmitting news to the far corners of the globe. 

Also, Outbreak - (www.outbreak.org), which TR calls the "single best site on the Web for one-stop surfing on emerging diseases." 

- Bandwidth's New Bargaineers - A report on the possibility that bandwidth will soon be a tradable commodity along with crude oil, cocoa beans and porkbellies. Companies leading the way are listed in feature. 

- Egghead Goes Virtual - The story of how Egghead Computer transformed itself into a virtual company. The article deals with the challenges and difficulties of an electronic commerce business. 

For full-text of these stories (for press only), please contact June Howlett, 781/237-2347, or e-mail: ja_Howlett@compuserve.com. The magazine will be available on newsstands Oct. 27, 1998 and can be read on-line at www.techreview.com. 

Technology Review will celebrate its 100th anniversary next year, it is the oldest technology magazine in the world. Relaunched this year as "MIT's Magazine of Innovation," Technology Review focuses on the latest, most important technological innovations across a wide range of fields, including biotech, nanotech and information technology. Published by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Technology Review now serves a greatly expanded audience, providing information and analysis of leading-edge discoveries and their potential impact on science, business and society.

Zygo Announces First Quarter Fiscal 1999 Results 

1,301 words 
26 October 1998
21:19 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

MIDDLEFIELD, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 26, 1998--Zygo Corporation (NASDAQ:ZIGO) today announced its financial results for the first quarter of fiscal 1999, ended September 30, 1998. In announcing its results, Gary K. Willis, president and CEO of Zygo, stated, "while economic conditions continued to impact orders from our two largest market sectors, semiconductor and data storage, our order rates improved from the fourth quarter of fiscal 1998. Despite these difficult conditions, the Company was essentially able to break even prior to charges recorded as a result of the bankruptcy filing of a data storage customer, and we made substantial progress in our strategy of delivering integrated metrology-based yield improvement solutions to the production floor of our customers by booking several large orders in the quarter." 

Net sales in the three months ended September 30, 1998 totaled $15,438,000, a decrease of $8,878,000 or 37% from $24,316,000 in the three months ended September 30, 1997. Net sales of the Company's instruments and systems decreased by 45% to approximately $9,412,000 and net sales of its modules and components totaled approximately $6,026,000 a decrease of 15% from the comparable quarter in the prior year. Net sales of both instruments and systems and modules and components were significantly impacted by the prolonged downturn in the semiconductor and data storage industries. 

The Company recorded a net loss of $1,071,000 in the three months ended September 30, 1998 versus net income of $1,698,000 in the year earlier period ended September 30, 1997 which included $1,920,000 of nonrecurring charges. The net loss in the most recent quarter was largely due to the reversal of revenues and establishment of an allowance for doubtful accounts relating to contracts in process with StorMedia Inc. and its affiliates which filed for Chapter 11 protection with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court on October 11, 1998. The Company, therefore, essentially produced breakeven results on substantially lower revenues. This financial performance was positively impacted by the cost reduction actions taken late in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1998 and early in the first quarter of fiscal 1999. Commenting on these results, Mr. Willis stated, "management has focused considerable attention on ensuring that appropriate cost reduction measures are implemented, while at the same time investing in those activities that have the greatest long-term benefit to the Company." Mr. Willis added, "one example of these investments was the distribution agreement signed with IBM which allows the Company to add Atomic Force Microscopy to our array of measurement technologies and to further our claim of the broadest measurement capability among metrology suppliers to high technology markets today." The net loss on a per share basis was $(.10) for the quarter ending September 30, 1998 compared with net earnings per share in the comparable prior year period of $.14 which included certain nonrecurring charges. 

Backlog at September 30, 1998 totaled $25,520,000, an increase of $1,110,000 or 5% from June 30, 1998 and a decrease of $18,245,000 or 42% from September 30, 1997. While the Company continued to experience softness in demand in the first quarter for its instruments and systems due to very difficult market conditions in the semiconductor and data storage markets, the Company had a positive book-to-bill ratio at 1.07 in the quarter ended September 30, 1998. 

Commenting on the outlook for the Company, Mr. Willis stated, "while sales of the Company's products remain somewhat dependent upon macro economic conditions in the markets the Company serves, which can not be accurately predicted, the Company's strong financial position and actions taken by the Company to reduce our cost structure and broaden our technology, market and product base, should allow us to improve our competitive position and financial performance in the future as these depressed markets improve." 

Zygo Corporation designs, develops, manufactures, and markets high performance measurement and yield improvement instruments, systems, and accessories used in high technology industries. The Company is headquartered in Middlefield, Connecticut, and also has operations in Asslar, Germany; Longmont, Colorado; and in Newbury Park and Sunnyvale, California. Zygo is traded on the Nasdaq National Market under the symbol ZIGO. Additional information on the Company is available on the Internet at www.zygo.com.

SangStat Receives Second Cyclosporine US Patent; Covers Newly FDA Approved SangCya 

1,084 words 
3 November 1998
16:47 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

MENLO PARK, Calif.--(BW HealthWire)--Nov. 3, 1998--SangStat, The Transplant Company(R), (Nasdaq:SANG), announced today that the United States Patent and Trademark Office has issued Patent No. 5,827,822, SangStat's second patent covering the company's proprietary cyclosporine formulation technology for developing multiple formulations and dosage forms of cyclosporine. SangCya(TM) (Cyclosporine Oral Solution, USP (MODIFIED)), the company's first product covered by this patent, was just approved (see separate press release issued today) by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as a bioequivalent formulation to Neoral(R) oral solution for the prevention of rejection in organ transplant recipients. 

"We are extremely pleased to have received this second broad patent at the time of SangCya market approval," said Philippe Pouletty, MD, Chairman and CEO of SangStat. "We are building a strong patent portfolio for SangCya and our other cyclosporine product candidates. Our first patent issued in June covers the cyclosporine formulation composition and this second patent covers the physical properties of cyclosporine upon oral administration of the formulation." 

Cyclosporine is a hydrophobic molecule, meaning that in its native form it exhibits poor solubility, absorption from the GI tract, and bioavailability. The allowed claims under the new patent cover cyclosporine formulations formed as a microdispersion in aqueous fluids. This technology refers to the formation of cyclosporine nanoparticles for oral administration. The gut easily absorbs nanoparticles, allowing cyclosporine release and circulation in the bloodstream n this process is called microdispersion. The new patent follows SangStat's first cyclosporine patent, issued in June 1998 (No. 5,766,629), which describes and covers multiple formulations, per the characteristics of the inactive ingredients combined with cyclosporine into specific pharmaceutical formulations. Under certain conditions, such formulations can promote the formation of nanoparticles when contacted with an aqueous medium, such as a beverage or gastric juice (patent No. 5,827,822). These proprietary formulation technologies enable cyclosporine to be absorbed while stable and suitable for use in various dosage forms, including oral solution and hard gel capsules. 


Cyclosporine Market


Cyclosporine is the leading immunosuppressive drug used in transplantation to prevent graft rejection. In addition to SangStat's SangCya, which SangStat intends to launch in the US within a month, cyclosporine is marketed by Novartis Ltd. in different formulations as Sandimmune(R) and Neoral with estimated worldwide sales of $1.3 billion in 1997. In the U.S. and Europe there are more than 240,000 transplant recipients requiring daily immunosuppressive therapy for the rest of their lives, the majority of whom take cyclosporine. 


Cyclosporine Development Program


SangStat and its collaborators investigated more than 200 formulations of cyclosporine in order to select the candidates that would be stable, highly bioavailable and therefore well absorbed, and outside the numerous cyclosporine formulation and process patents that exist. While the research on the composition of the formulations and clinical development was mostly conducted by SangStat and its collaborators in the US, the research on the microdispersion technology was primarily conducted by SangStat's French research subsidiary, SangStat Atlantique, in Nantes, and involved several academic collaborators. Of SangStat's 273 original cyclosporine formulations, 40 were tested in pre-clinical models, 16 were then tested in pilot human trials before an optimal candidate, SangCya, was selected for use in pivotal human trials. SangStat investigators and scientists have presented the results of the Company's pivotal bioequivalence trials and patient pharmacokinetic conversion trials at several US and international scientific meetings (J Clin Pharmacol 1998 Sept;38(9):807; Transplantation 1998;65(12):S13 and S66; Transplant Proc 1998, 30:1701). SangCya is now approved for marketing in the US (please refer to the separate press release issued today). In February 1998, SangStat filed for marketing authorization for cyclosporine in Europe and the application is under active review. Additional cyclosporine dosage forms (capsules) are being developed for similar indications. 


The Company


SangStat is a specialty pharmaceutical company applying a disease management approach to improve the outcome of organ transplantation. SangStat has a total of 12 monitoring and therapeutic product and product candidates to address the pre-transplant, acute care and chronic phases of transplantation. SangStat is in Menlo Park, California, and operates The Transplant Pharmacy(R) a comprehensive pharmacotherapy management program, and wholly-owned subsidiaries IMTIX-SangStat, SangStat's European base of operations in Lyon, France; SangStat Canada, Ltd. in Mississauga, Ontario, Canada; and Human Organ Sciences(TM), Inc., in Menlo Park, California.

Sangstat Medical Corporation Reports Third Quarter 1998 Results 

1,509 words 
16 November 1998
11:13 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(c) 1998 Business Wire

MENLO PARK, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 16, 1998--SangStat, The Transplant Company(R), (Nasdaq:SANG), today reported a net loss of $13,593,000 or $0.84 per share for the third quarter of 1998. This compares with a net loss of $5,202,000 or $0.33 per share for the third quarter of 1997. This loss included a one time charge to earnings of $3,219,000 or $0.20 per share relating to the write-off of in-process research and development purchased as part of the IMTIX acquisition. Excluding this one-time charge, the net loss would have been $10,375,000 or $0.64 per share. At September 30, 1998, SangStat had cash, cash equivalents, and investments of $50,801,000. 

Total revenues in the third quarter of 1998 were $3,028,000, a 169% increase over revenues of $1,127,000 in the third quarter of 1997. Revenues for the third quarter of 1998 consisted of $2,441,000 of Transplant Pharmacy revenues; $346,000 of therapeutic revenues (primarily THYMOGLOBULIN(R) sales in Canada under that country's emergency drug release program); $187,000 of monitoring product sales; and $54,000 of collaborative and licensing payments. 

Research, development, regulatory and clinical expenses were $4,801,000 in the third quarter of 1998, an increase of 7% versus the third quarter of 1997. These expenses mainly reflect the ongoing and newly initiated clinical trials in transplant patients with several cyclosporine dosage forms, THYMOGLOBULIN, ongoing development of monitoring devices, CELSIOR(R), AZATHIOPRINE, ALLOTRAP(R) peptides and XENOJECT(TM). 

Selling, general and administrative expenses were $6,478,000 in third quarter 1998 as compared to $2,945,000 in third quarter 1997. The increase mainly reflects the Company's build-up of its commercial infrastructure, and pre-launch activities to help support the US launch of SangCya' ("sang-see-ah"), SangStat's cyclosporine which was granted marketing approval by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on October 31, 1998, and the future potential US launch of THYMOGLOBULIN, subject to regulatory approval. This included the expansion of the North American marketing, sales and customer service departments to a total of 35 people including a sales force of 21 representatives, and continued personnel additions to support the growing number of patients and centers participating in The Transplant Pharmacy(R) program. 

Several significant milestones were achieved both during the third quarter and in the subsequent months, including the recent FDA marketing approval of SangCya, the issuance of an additional patent covering SangStat's proprietary cyclosporine formulations, the 510(k) clearance of CycloTech' and the closing of the acquisition of IMTIX-SangStat. 


SangStat Received US FDA Marketing Approval of SangCya (Cyclosporine
Oral Solution, USP (MODIFIED) 100 mg/mL).


On October 31, 1998, the FDA granted marketing approval to SangCya(TM) (Cyclosporine Oral Solution, USP (MODIFIED), 100 mg/mL) for prevention of rejection in solid organ transplant recipients, and an AB rating versus Neoral(R) oral solution. SangCya is SangStat's patented formulation of cyclosporine, previously known by the research code name Sang-35. SangCya is the first therapeutically equivalent competitor to be introduced in the $500 million US cyclosporine marketplace. SangStat developed SangCya after evaluating over 270 cyclosporine formulations. The result was the development of a patented product that was shown in human trials to be bioequivalent to Neoral, the newer formulation of cyclosporine marketed by Novartis. 


SangStat Received Second Cyclosporine US Patent - Covers Newly FDA
Approved SangCya(TM)


On November 3, SangStat announced that the United States Patent and Trademark Office had issued Patent No. 5,827,822, SangStat's second patent covering the company's proprietary cyclosporine formulation technology for developing multiple formulations and dosage forms of cyclosporine. 

Cyclosporine is a hydrophobic molecule, meaning that in its native form it exhibits poor solubility, absorption from the gastrointestinal tract, and bioavailability. The allowed claims under the new patent cover cyclosporine formulations formed as a microdispersion in aqueous fluids. This technology refers to the formation of cyclosporine nanoparticles for oral administration. The gut easily absorbs nanoparticles, allowing cyclosporine release and circulation in the bloodstream n this process is called microdispersion. The new patent follows SangStat's first cyclosporine patent, issued in June 1998 (#5,766,629), which describes and covers multiple formulations, per the characteristics of the inactive ingredients combined with cyclosporine into specific pharmaceutical formulations. Under certain conditions, such formulations can promote the formation of nanoparticles when contacted with an aqueous medium such as a beverage or gastric juice (patent #5,827,822). These proprietary formulation technologies enable cyclosporine to be absorbed while stable and suitable for use in various dosage forms, including oral solution and hard gel capsules. 


SangStat Received Marketing Clearance (510k) for CycloTech(TM)


On August 24, SangStat received marketing clearance (510k) for CycloTech(TM). CycloTech is a hand-held device that is designed to deliver and track each dose of SangCya taken by a transplant recipient. 

Although SangCya can be taken alone, SangStat intends to offer the CycloTech device, as a free of charge option, to individual transplant recipients taking SangCya. Approximately the size of a cell phone, CycloTech was designed to help recipients manage and track their daily dosing regimen. It can then be connected to a computer to help physicians and transplant coordinators monitor drug usage. Transplant recipients using cyclosporine usually must take the drug every day for the rest of their lives to reduce the chances of organ rejection by the body's immune system. 


SangStat And Pasteur Merieux Connaught (Rhone-Poulenc Group) Announced
The Closing Of SangStat's Acquisition Of IMTIX, Pasteur Merieux
Connaught's Transplant Division


On October 1, SangStat and Pasteur Merieux Connaught (Rhone-Poulenc Group) announced the closing of the acquisition of Pasteur Merieux Connaught's organ transplant business known as IMTIX. The resulting wholly owned subsidiary of SangStat, named IMTIX-SangStat, is dedicated to the development, manufacturing and sale of transplantation products in more than 60 countries outside of North America, primarily in Europe. 

SangStat acquired IMTIX for $31 million, which consisted of $10 million paid upon closing and $21 million payable over five years. In addition, SangStat will pay Pasteur Merieux Connaught royalties on IMTIX-SangStat product sales that are variable and contingent upon the sales of certain IMTIX-SangStat products. Costs relating to this acquisition were approximately $2 million. The transaction will be accounted for using the purchase method. 

"The recent FDA marketing approval of SangCya has marked SangStat's transition from the development to the commercial stage," said Philippe Pouletty, M.D., Chairman and CEO. "With our continued growth and expected near term approval of THYMOGLOBULIN we believe that by the end of 1999, we will report our first profitable quarter." 


SangStat, The Transplant Company(R)


SangStat is a specialty pharmaceutical company applying a disease management approach to improve the outcome of organ transplantation. SangStat has a total of 12 monitoring and therapeutic products and product candidates to address the pre-transplant, acute care and chronic phases of transplantation. SangStat received FDA marketing approval for SangCya (Cyclosporine Oral Solution, USP (MODIFIED) 100 mg/mL) in October 1998. SangStat is based in Menlo Park, California, and operates The Transplant Pharmacy, a comprehensive pharmacotherapy management program, and wholly owned subsidiaries, IMTIX-SangStat, SangStat's European base of operations in Lyon, France, SangStat Canada, Ltd. in Mississauga, Ontario, Canada and Human Organ Sciences(TM), in Menlo Park, California.
