The company is planning to invest $41.6 million in this project, including the land, building, machinery and equipment. 

"Nanovation Technologies is exactly the type of high-tech employer we are striving to attract to our great state," said Governor John Engler. "Attracting this state-of-the-art company puts further fuel in Michigan's high-tech engine." 

Nanovation's Northville Facility, located at 47050 Five Mile Road, Northville Township Mich., is eventually expected to house up to 539 employees, which will make it one of the largest area employers. 

"The facility purchase gives Nanovation the flexibility to determine the most cost-effective way to meet market demands for our highly integrated photonics products at any given time," said G. Robert Tatum, Nanovation president and chief executive officer. "As this facility was already outfitted with state-of-the-art manufacturing equipment, we expect to save at least a year in making our products commercially available." 

The Governor announced an approval of a Michigan Economic Growth Authority (MEGA) tax credit worth an estimated $9.7 million over 11 years to Nanovation Technologies, resulting in a net positive gain for the state of $35.3 million after tax credits. 

The new manufacturing facility will provide more than $45 million in revenue to the state over the life of the agreement and $563 million in personal income during that time. 

As part of its commitment to the State of Michigan, Nanovation also announced that the Michigan-based Princeton Capital Fund has committed to invest in the company. "We believe that Nanovation Technologies has the right approach, technology, products and management team to offer the integrated components that provide the most complete solution in a photonics switching environment," said Daniel Dorman, President of Princeton Capital Fund, LLC. "Through its proprietary relationships with Northwestern University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the company is not only developing products that meet market needs today, it is concentrating on next generation technology and products." 

Situated on 20 acres, the 4-year-old plant includes premier clean rooms vital for the semiconductor manufacturing of nanophotonic devices, as well as space for engineering development, R&D, prototype construction, assembly and test, environmental screening, offices and shipping and receiving. The site is large enough to accommodate future campus style expansions. 

This internal resource will be used to implement Nanovation's strategic plan to meet expected market demands as telecommunications companies and other network providers begin to upgrade their networks to offer users substantially greater capacity. Nanovation's integrated optical components eliminate the inherent inefficiencies of opto-electronic-based components, which hinder the speed, and capacity of today's networks. 

About Nanovation Technologies Inc. 

Nanovation Technologies is dedicated to designing and developing customized integrated optical devices and discrete components for the explosive fiber communications market. Its first-generation product portfolio is based on truly integrated, high performance optical components including switches, splitters, couplers and monitoring taps that offer significant price and performance advantages as well as a complete line of EDFA products. Headquartered in Miami, the company also has laboratories at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Northwestern University; a manufacturing facility located in Northville Township, Mich.; as well as its subsidiary, Apollo Photonics, based in Burlington, Ontario, Canada.            In the second quarter of 2000, ABB entered an alliance with
PaperLoop.com (www.paperloop.com), an online paper industry
marketplace, to jointly develop a new Web portal for the pulp and
paper industry. ABB said development is aimed at creating a portal to
put technical information databases online, offer consulting services
via the Web, and provide industrial software that customers can
download or use directly online.
           In May, ABB acquired a minority stake in Capclear
(www.capclear.com), an Internet-based clearinghouse for
business-to-business Internet exchanges. Their services minimize risks
and reduce transaction costs of Internet trade.
           As previously announced, ABB intends to invest US$ 1 billion in
Industrial IT, eBusiness and related activities by the end of 2001,
and have 30 percent of its standard products and services online by
the end of this year and 100 percent by the end of next year. Further,
ABB expects to significantly expand its Web-based product and service
offerings to a number of key customers this year.
Alternative energy
           In June, ABB launched a new business to deliver alternative energy
solutions worldwide. Demand for alternative energy sources and
small-scale power generation - wind farms, fuel cells, combined heat
and power plants using miniature gas turbines - has been sparked by
deregulation, forcing power suppliers to put a higher priority on
profitability. Small-scale power, because it requires less up-front
capital investment, often meets this need better than conventional
large power plants. In addition, governments around the world have
committed to cut greenhouse gas emissions in line with the 1997 Kyoto
Protocol on global warming, which also promotes small-scale
alternative energy solutions.
           In anticipation of this growing demand, ABB unveiled its new wind
power technology, called the Windformer(TM). The Windformer will
enable the economical development of wind farms with outputs up to 300
megawatts (MW) or more - equivalent to a medium-sized fossil-fuel
power plant.
           The Windformer also reduces power losses and can be used to
connect wind farms directly to larger power grids, even from offshore.
ABB is also working with DuPont (USA) to develop a more complete fuel
cell solution and Volvo (Sweden) to market a smaller, smarter and more
powerful microturbine.
           ABB said the US$ 100 million order to build natural gas-fired CHP
plants - small-scale units that produce both electricity and heat -
over the next 1 1/2 years throughout the U.K., confirmed the move into
alternative energy solutions.
Bringing new technologies to market
           In addition to breakthroughs in alternative energy, ABB is the
leading developer of technology in areas like oil, gas and
petrochemicals, sensors and analytical systems, software engineering,
power electronics, and microengineering and nanotechnologies.
           ABB supplied the drilling riser, wellhead and blowout preventer
control system for the world's deepest subsea well, 2,777 meters
beneath the sea off the coast of Brazil. ABB also started up and is
operating the world's first subsea separator at Norsk Hydro's Troll
Field off the coast of Norway. The system separates water from the oil
stream and injects it back to the well. It can improve oil recovery
rates by as much as 50 percent and reduces environmental impacts,
lowering total field investment, operating costs and development time.
           In the growing market for analytic systems for food and beverages,
and pharmaceuticals, ABB launched infrared testing systems that allow
fast sampling of a large number of substances. ABB has applied its
micro-engineered catalyst technology to the environmental control
field. A test reactor has been installed to improve the performance of
a high-dust pollution control unit at a 2000-megawatt (MW) coal-fired
power plant in the U.S.
           To open new markets in remote monitoring and control of power
distribution networks, ABB launched a substation design that boasts an
integrated Web server and a wireless communication system. The product
allows an operator to monitor and control the substation via the
Internet.
           ABB's breakthrough Azipod technology, an electrical propulsion
system for ships with a 360-degree steering angle, is now available
for smaller ships in the power range up to 5 megawatts (MW). This
technology, which helps navigate many of the largest ships around the
world, captures both simplicity of design and strength of
functionality.
Cash Flow and other key data
           In line with ABB's ongoing efforts to create more value through
higher cash flow generation, net cash flow from operating activities
increased by 46 percent compared to first six months 1999, reaching
US$ 413 million (1999: US$ 282 million).
           The return on capital employed for the first six months 2000
reached 17.0 percent (1999: 16.0 percent) and return on equity
improved to 34.4 percent (1999: 30.8 percent). The order backlog
amounted to US$ 14,906 million at end of June (December 31, 1999: US$
13,245 million).
           The number of employees at the end of June was 161,401 (end of
June 1999: 174,601). Adjusted for acquisitions and divestitures, the
number of employees decreased by 5 percent.
Segment and regional review
           ABB Group reports in U.S. dollars and the strengthening dollar had
a major negative effect on the reported figures for the first half
year 2000 when translated from local currencies. The following
discussion refers to the development in local currencies.
           Power Transmission orders rebounded on improved conditions in most
major markets during the second quarter. Several large interconnection
projects came to fruition and ABB capitalized on increased demand for
power transformers and service and support. The operating margin
improved to 11.4 percent from 10.5 percent last year. Earnings for the
segment were flat, reflecting the divestiture last year of the
standard cable business. Deregulation is now beginning to fuel demand
in the power transmission market, as it has already done in the power
distribution sector. Although demand may be sluggish in the first
phase of deregulation, as customers are cautious with investments in
an uncertain market, it is expected to grow rapidly in continental
Europe. This is especially true in service, retrofit and IT
applications, where customers can obtain good return on investments
while optimizing the use of existing assets.
           Deregulation continued to fuel the Power Distribution business as
orders and earnings increased substantially, 23 percent and 25
percent, respectively. Orders were supported by strong demand for
intelligent system solutions and transformers. The operating margin
increased to 7.5 percent from 6.9 percent last year. Demand for
products, services and solutions continued to grow, especially in
North America. The business also experienced strong demand in Asia,
where economic recovery continues.
           Earnings in Automation were up 27 percent, driven by the
successful integration of Elsag Bailey, higher value projects and
improved demand for instrumentation and control products. The segment
also reduced its cost base substantially and continued to improve
internal efficiency and quality management. Operating margins were
sharply higher, 8.6 percent compared to 6.7 percent for the first six
months of 1999. Orders were about 8 percent higher in all major
businesses, driven by improved demand in the U.S., Europe and Asia.
The product business showed strong growth in all regions, while the
large project business was still weak.
           Oil, Gas and Petrochemicals' orders continued to surge - up 47
percent - in large part reflecting higher demand in the downstream
petrochemicals market. As forecast, earnings suffered from last year's
low order intake. The operating margin was slightly up at 5.8 percent
compared to 5.5 percent the first six months of 1999. The increased
orders should flow through to revenues in the fourth quarter of this
year and in particular in 2001. Higher bidding activity in both
upstream and downstream markets indicates that demand should remain
robust for the rest of the year.
           Earnings for Building Technologies increased 12 percent.
Low-voltage products and systems benefited from improved demand. The
operating margin reached 7.4 percent compared to 6.8 for the previous
year. Orders were up 7 percent, with increased order intake in all
business areas, however the service business area lagged in orders and
revenues due to periodization of several large full service contracts.
The markets in the Asia, Middle East and Africa showed good growth and
our markets for installation of Internet and mobile telecommunications
systems are growing rapidly. The shift from low-margin general
contracting to high-tech installations is continuing.
           Financial Services' earnings were in line with last year's level.
The segment continued its strategy to invest in fast-growing knowledge
and Internet-based businesses. The acquisition of the share of SEK
supports the segment's specialization in long-term export finance and
finance solutions to sectors such as telecommunications, automotive,
transportation, energy, and process industries like pulp and paper and
petrochemicals. SEK employs some 90 people and has total assets of
approximately US$ 20 billion, mostly representing securities with bank
or government guarantees.
           European markets continued to improve, with orders up 14 percent
in local currencies. Most major markets in Central and Southern Europe
showed strong growth. Asia's orders rebounded during the second
quarter, particularly the product business. But over the first six
months, orders were down compared to last year, when several large
orders were recorded in the corresponding period. The Middle East and
Africa showed good growth, with increased activities in product and
service businesses. Demand in North America continued to grow, with
the liberalization of the power market pushing orders higher. In the
deregulated markets of South America, demand continued to grow for
regional power interconnections and demand in product businesses
improved greatly.
Change in accounting
           During the second quarter of 2000, ABB disposed of the former
Power Generation segment, which included its investment in ABB ALSTOM
POWER N.V. and its nuclear business. According to International
Accounting Standards (IAS), disposing of a business segment should be
accounted for as discontinued operations. Accordingly, the after-tax
income of the former Power Generation segment has been combined into a
single line in the Income Statement called "Income from discontinued
operations, net of tax" for both 2000 and 1999, respectively. Also
included in this line are capital gains, net of tax, from the
disposition of the Power Generation segment (in 2000 and 1999) and
Adtranz (in 1999), previously reported in Operating Earnings as
"unusual items."
Outlook
           For the full-year 2000, ABB's orders are expected to show a good
increase. Revenues in the second half are expected to increase
compared to the same period last year. Operating earnings are expected
to increase from last year's level and net income will continue to be
well above 1999's performance. Cash flow from operating activities is
expected to grow faster than operating earnings as the Value Based
Management initiative, including the capital reduction program, is
further gaining pace. The power generation and nuclear divestitures do
not affect the outlook negatively for this year, nor the longer-term
targets of 6-7 percent average annual growth during 2000-2003 and an
operating margin of 12 percent by 2003.
The ABB Group serves customers in power transmission and
distribution; automation; oil, gas, and petrochemicals; building
technologies; and in financial services. With novel IT applications,
tailored software solutions, growing eBusiness and a fast-expanding
knowledge and service base, ABB is building links to the new economy.
The ABB Group employs about 160,000 people in more than 100 countries.

Veeco Reports Second Quarter and Six Month Results; Record Second Quarter Sales and Bookings; Explosive Optical Telecommunications Activity 

1,950 words 
27 July 2000
23:32 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(Copyright (c) 2000, Business Wire) 

PLAINVIEW, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--July 27, 2000--Veeco Instruments Inc. (NASDAQ:VECO) today announced its financial results for the quarter and six months ended June 30, 2000. Historical results have been restated to include the merger with CVC, Inc., which closed on May 5, 2000 and was accounted for as a pooling of interests. 

Second Quarter Results 

Sales for the second quarter of 2000 were a record $93.6 million, a 21% increase over the $77.1 million reported in the second quarter of 1999. Veeco's Process Equipment sales were $47.6 million, unchanged from the second quarter of last year. Second quarter Metrology sales were a record $43.1 million, a 69% increase over the $25.5 million reported in the second quarter of 1999. Metrology growth included increased sales of atomic force microscopes to the semiconductor market, and sales of Veeco's new optical metrology products for the data storage industry. 

Bookings for the second quarter of 2000 were a record $132.4 million, a 65% increase over the $80.5 million in the second quarter of 1999. Veeco's Process Equipment bookings were $83.6 million, a 62% increase over the $51.7 million in the second quarter of 1999, including increases in both optical telecommunications and data storage bookings. Veeco's Ion Tech subsidiary, which manufactures optical coating ion beam deposition systems used by manufacturers of Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) filters, reported a 227% increase in second quarter bookings to $38.9 million from $11.9 million in the prior year second quarter. Process Equipment bookings for Plainview and Rochester combined etch and deposition equipment increased 12% to $44.6 million from $39.8 million in the prior year second quarter. Veeco's second quarter Metrology bookings increased 82% to $46.2 million from the $25.3 million in the second quarter of 1999; including a 74% increase in atomic force microscopes and a 98% increase in optical metrology products. Veeco's family of automated semiconductor metrology tools (Vx Atomic Force Profiler and the Dimension 9000 Atomic Force Microscope) reported strong second quarter orders due to their recent adoption by leading semiconductor manufacturers. Veeco's second quarter book/bill ratio was 1.41. 

Veeco's second quarter 2000 operating income was $7.8 million (excluding non-recurring charges) compared with $11.8 million in the second quarter of 1999. In conjunction with the merger with CVC, Veeco incurred second quarter non-recurring charges of $33.0 million. Of these charges, $15.3 million related to a write off of inventory (included in cost of sales), $14.0 million of merger and reorganization costs (of which $9.2 million related to transaction costs and $4.8 million pertained to duplicate facility and personnel costs) and $3.7 million was for the write-down of long-lived assets. Net income was $5.1 million in the second quarter of 2000 (excluding non-recurring charges), versus $7.7 million in the corresponding period of last year. Diluted earnings per share for the second quarter of 2000 were $0.21 per share (excluding non-recurring charges) compared to $0.36 per share in the second quarter of 1999. Veeco's decline in profitability in 2000 versus the prior year is primarily attributable to the lower gross margins experienced in the Company's data storage Process Equipment businesses. 

First Half Results 

Veeco's sales for the first half of 2000 were $171.5 million, a 13% increase over the $151.6 million for the first half of 1999. Process Equipment first half sales increased 8% to $91.9 million, compared to $85.4 million in the first half of last year. First half 2000 Metrology sales were a record $74.0 million, a 31% increase over the $56.4 million in the first half of 1999. 

Veeco's first half 2000 bookings were a record $243.6 million, a 40% increase over the $174.1 million in the first half of 1999. Process Equipment first half bookings were a record $144.2 million, a 24% increase over the $116.5 million reported in the first half of 1999. First half 2000 Metrology bookings increased 86% to a record $93.6 million from the $50.3 million last year. Veeco's six-month book/bill ratio was 1.42. 

In the first half of 2000, Veeco's operating income was $11.4 million (excluding non-recurring charges related to the CVC merger and previously announced charges related to the merger with Monarch Labs) compared to $21.9 million in the first half of 1999. Net income in the first half of 2000 was $7.7 million (excluding non-recurring charges) compared to $13.8 million last year. Excluding non-recurring charges, diluted earnings per share in the first six months of 2000 was $0.31 per share compared to $0.66 per share last year. Veeco's decline in profitability in 2000 versus the prior year is primarily attributable to the lower gross margins experienced in the Company's data storage Process Equipment businesses. 

Management Review of Results 

Regarding these results, Edward H. Braun, Veeco's Chairman and CEO commented, "Veeco's record second quarter orders of $132.4 million and record sales of $93.6 million reflect the strength of our optical telecommunications deposition equipment, semiconductor metrology products and new data storage products, and the overall growth of these information age markets. All of Veeco's Process Equipment and Metrology product lines experienced order increases. 

"Veeco's second quarter orders from the optical telecommunications market were over $45.0 million ($38.9 million from Ion Tech), representing 34% of the Company's total bookings," Mr. Braun continued. "Going forward, it is our intention to become a leading one-stop supplier of etch, deposition and metrology equipment to the optical telecommunications marketplace by leveraging our technology and strong customer relationships. Our Metrology orders for the second quarter were $46.2 million, up 82% over last year's second quarter, driven by our automated semiconductor atomic force metrology tools." 

During the second quarter, Veeco completed its merger with CVC, Inc. Mr. Braun commented, "By combining the technologies of Veeco and CVC, we are now able to offer data storage manufacturers the most advanced, fully integrated process equipment systems for their next generation 50 to 100Gb/in2 giant magnetoresistive (GMR) thin film head development projects. As a result, Veeco received a $5.0 million order in the second quarter from a leading U.S. hard drive manufacturer for an integrated 10-target ultra-high vacuum, combined physical vapor deposition (PVD) and ion beam deposition tool to be used in the development of advanced high density GMR thin film magnetic heads. In addition, our merger with CVC provides an expanded PVD product line for the active device optical telecommunications market." Mr. Braun added, "Veeco's integration of CVC and previously announced cost reductions are expected to favorably impact second half profitability." 

About Veeco 

Veeco Instruments Inc. is a worldwide leader in process equipment and metrology tools for the optical telecommunications, data storage, semiconductor and research markets. Manufacturing and engineering facilities are located in New York, California, Colorado, Arizona and Minnesota. Global sales and service offices are located throughout the United States, Europe, Japan and Asia Pacific. Additional information on Veeco can be found at http://www.veeco.com.

These factors include the cyclical nature of the data storage, optical telecommunications and semiconductor industries, risks associated with the acceptance of new products by individual customers and by the marketplace, and other factors discussed in the Business Description and Management's Discussion and Analysis sections of Veeco's Report on Form 10-K and Annual Report to Shareholders.

Mitsubishi Corp., MER and RCT Form Company to Commercialize Fullerenes

639 words 
31 July 2000
11:19 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(Copyright (c) 2000, Business Wire) 

TUCSON, Ariz.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--July 31, 2000--Since the discovery a decade ago of a simple way to produce macroscopic quantities of fullerenes, the challenge has been to find practical uses for the carbon molecules and to scale up production economically. 

Fullerene International Corp. (FIC) combines the capabilities of partners Mitsubishi Corp. (MC), Materials and Electrochemical Research Corp. (MER), and Research Corporation Technologies (RCT) in a joint venture to commercialize fullerene materials. 

MC, the giant trading company, brings business development and market incubation to FIC. MER, a high technology development company in Tucson, provides production, production scale-up, application development, technical support and patents to the new company. RCT, a Tucson-based intellectual property management company, contributes dominant composition-of-matter and method-of-production patents. 

FIC first established a fullerene manufacturing facility in Japan. Dr. Raouf O. Loutfy, MER president and FIC chief operations officer, said MER built a scaled-up reactor and separation system for FIC subcontractor Honjo Chemical Corp., a specialty chemical company in Osaka, Japan. 

Following complete system optimization and training by MER, Loutfy said, Honjo should be a supplier of fullerenes materials in Asia by this fall. 

Simultaneously, FIC will form collaborations with several Japanese companies to explore the potential use of the hollow, cage-shaped molecules in a diverse range of products. The initial targeted applications for fullerenes include batteries, field electron displays, gas storage, diamond-like cutting tools, capacitors for electric vehicles, sports equipment and pharmaceuticals. 

"The business model of FIC is a new direction for MC," said FIC President and Chief Executive Officer Susumu Katagiri, who also is manager in MC's technology and business development department in Tokyo. 

"The new business vision of MC," said MC President Mikio Sasaki, "is leveraging advanced technologies into dynamic new ventures." 

MER in Tucson has been producing fullerenes and nanotubes, and developing applications for these unique materials since their discovery. In the last five years, MER and MC have been evaluating the commercial potential of fullerene materials in Japan. They found commercial potential limited by commercial-scale production levels and cost. 

FIC plans to scale up production in Japan, identify lowest-production-cost technology and promote commercial applications. 

Besides its work with fullerenes, MER also develops high-technology materials such as advanced composites, powders, coatings and energy conversion systems including batteries, fuel cells and gas-storage systems. 

RCT has managed commercialization of the fullerene technology since its invention in September 1990 by physicists Donald R. Huffman at the University of Arizona and Wolfgang Kratschmer at the Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics in Heidelberg, Germany. 

In this technique, graphite rods are evaporated in a helium atmosphere to produce fullerene materials, the third form of carbon besides diamonds and graphite. RCT filed for worldwide patent protection of both carbon 60 (C60) and carbon 70 (C70), and the general techniques for making the compounds. 

Composition of matter and method of production patents have issued in Australia, Japan, Europe and South Korea. Similar patent applications are pending in the United States. 

Companies or research groups interested in collaborating with FIC should contact Katagiri at FIC, c/o Mitsubishi International Corp. Planning and Coordination Division (MIC/PCD), 520 Madison Ave., New York, NY 10022-4223, 212/605-2286, 212/605-1847 fax, skatagiri@fullereneinternational.com; and Loutfy at MER, 7960 S. Kolb Road, Tucson, AZ, 85706, 520/574-1980, 520/574-1983 fax, rloutfy@fullereneinternational.com.

JMAR Technologies Reports Second Quarter Results; Losses Narrow from Prior Quarter 

1,455 words 
7 August 2000
13:46 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(Copyright (c) 2000, Business Wire) 

SAN DIEGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 7, 2000-- 

Resource Shift to Accelerate Launch of New High-Speed Semiconductor 

Chips Causes Temporary Sales Dip 

New Commercially Important Semiconductor Chip and Atomic Vision 

Product Launches are Imminent 

JMAR Technologies, Inc. (Nasdaq NM: JMAR), a provider of precision micro-technology products, today announced the results for its second quarter and six-months ended June 30, 2000. 

For the quarter, the company reported a net loss of $(198,030), or $(0.01) per share, compared to a net loss of $(263,953), or $(0.01) per share, in the quarter ended June 30, 1999, and compared with a net loss of $(580,596), or $(0.03), for the sequentially prior quarter ended March 31, 2000. Revenues for the quarter ended June 30, 2000 were $5,167,577 compared to $4,799,045 and $6,769,017 for the quarters ended March 31, 2000 and June 30, 1999, respectively. 

Commenting on the company's results, JMAR's Chairman and Chief Executive Officer John S. Martinez, Ph.D., said, "The difference in revenues for the 2000 quarter and six-month periods compared to 1999 was due to two factors: First, our sales in the corresponding 1999 periods contained large one-time contract revenues related to a semiconductor fabrication facility located in Sacramento, California that we developed and which we continue to support for the U.S. government under contract from a leading aerospace corporation. Second, starting in late 1999, we began to shift a portion of our engineering resources from contract revenue chip development work to internally-funded commercial chip development activities. That re-direction of effort was consistent with the Initiative that we announced on April 13, 2000 to accelerate JMAR's entry into the commercial telecom semiconductor product market. In the absence of these two factors, our second quarter revenues would have been approximately the same for each year." 

Dr. Martinez added, "Specific product introduction announcements related to our initial high-speed commercial semiconductor chip offerings will be forthcoming, shortly. As these new products gain acceptance in their respective marketplaces, we expect the aforementioned 'sales-dip' to be reversed." 

Dennis Valentine, JMAR's vice president and chief financial officer, commented, "Revenues and earnings continued to be affected adversely by our expanded commercial product development programs targeted at the semiconductor industry. At the same time, we are also seeing positive trends that indicate our efforts to improve future profitability are having the desired impact. For example, gross margins for the six-month period ending June 30, 2000 were 34.5%, up substantially from 27.0% for the prior year period, reflecting the continued resurgence of our Company's higher margin precision instrument products at JMAR Precision Systems (JPSI)." 

Mr. Valentine continued, "It is also important to note that the first six months of 2000 generated very positive results for our shareholders, both in terms of share price appreciation and the strengthening of our balance sheet. During that period the Company received net proceeds of approximately $16 million from the exercise of outstanding options and warrants, including its warrants which traded for seven years on the Nasdaq National Market System under the symbol: JMARW. Approximately $5 million of these funds were used to pay down, in its entirety, the Company's working capital line with Comerica Bank, thereby preserving the full Line for future use. We are investing another portion of these funds to accelerate the Company's development of new high-value semiconductor products for the rapidly growing telecommunications, data transfer and Internet markets and to accelerate the development and commercialization of some of our other high-value proprietary products." 

"During the past year we have worked diligently to strengthen our Microelectronics Equipment Business Segment activities, both in terms of technical and management expertise and new product offerings," Dr. Martinez noted. "Those efforts are starting to pay off by generating a broad new sales base for us, and by posturing JMAR to more effectively address the rapidly growing needs of the micro and nanotechnology segments of the semiconductor, biochip and fiber optics communications industries. During the second quarter, this highly positive trend produced several important new product offerings from JPSI, including a major line of nanometrology Atomic Vision(TM) instruments created by incorporating atomic force microscopy (AFM) technology into our existing Mirage(TM), Lumina(TM) and Z-Scope(TM) measurement systems. By doing so, we have increased the imaging resolution of our existing measurement products to better than one-one thousandth of a micron, or about one-one hundred thousandths of the thickness of a human hair." 

He continued, "We firmly believe that these new products, which we formally introduced to the industry in July 2000 at the Semicon West Trade Show in San Jose, CA and at two international expositions at the Taipai World Trade Center in Taiwan, will provide strong and exciting impetus to our entire precision measurement instrument business area in months to come. They are expected to have important manufacturing applications throughout the semiconductor, disk drive and microelectronics industries as well as for many biomedical research uses." 

Dr. Martinez also noted, "During this past quarter we took several major steps and made substantial progress toward strengthening and focusing JMAR's laser and X-ray source development and commercialization activities conducted by our Microelectronics Equipment Business Segment. All were the subject of prior press releases. One of the most noteworthy of them involved the award to JMAR, by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA), of an additional $3.8 million of contract funding to help transition our advanced X-ray lithography source development program to the prototype stage. We also announced an important financial, technical and marketing relationship with Bede Scientific Instruments Ltd. in Durham, U.K. to mutually broaden the commercial opportunities and applications for both of our companies' advanced X-ray technology products and services. And, we recently recruited Mr. John Carosella, former President of Osmic, Inc., a leading U.S. based X-ray optics products and technology company, to help provide JMAR with the management expertise and leadership to integrate these and other related activities into JMAR's current Advanced Light and precision instrument product lines. 

He concluded, "We, at JMAR are very encouraged with our progress since the start of this year and look forward to evaluating the commercial market reactions to our new semiconductor chip and equipment product introductions during the second half of 2000." 

JMAR Technologies Inc. is a leading developer of proprietary advanced laser and X-ray light sources for high-value microelectronics manufacturing and metrology.  Article 355 *******************    


Researchers From Lucent Technologies' Bell Labs and University of Oxford Create First DNA Motors 

993 words 
9 August 2000
18:30 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(Copyright (c) 2000, Business Wire) 

MURRAY HILL, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 9, 2000--Scientists from Bell Labs, the research and development arm of Lucent Technologies (NYSE: LU), and the University of Oxford have created the first DNA motors. The devices, which resemble motorized tweezers, are 100,000 times smaller than the head of a pin, and the techniques used to make them may lead to computers that are 1,000 times more powerful than today's machines. 

The DNA motor research, described in the August 10 issue of the British journal Nature, is part of a burgeoning field known as nanotechnology, where dimensions are on a nanometer scale - a billionth of a meter. Scientists believe nanoscale devices may lead to computer chips with billions of transistors, instead of millions - which is the typical range in today's semiconductor technology. The more transistors crammed on chip, the more powerful it is. 

"This technology has the potential to replace existing manufacturing methods for integrated circuits, which may reach their practical limits within the next decade when Moore's Law eventually hits a brick wall," said physicist Bernard Yurke of Bell Labs. 

DNA, which provides the molecular blueprints for all living cells, is an ideal tool for making nanoscale devices. "We took advantage of how pieces of DNA - with its billions of possible variations - lock together in only one particular way, like pieces of a jigsaw puzzle," Yurke said. 

The researchers designed pieces of synthetic DNA that would recognize each other during each step of making the DNA motors. As a result, the only necessary ingredients in a laboratory test tube were DNA itself. 

"Because DNA acts as the 'fuel' for these motors, they are completely self-sufficient and do not require other chemicals to operate, " Yurke said. 

The self-assembling aspect of the DNA motors also is crucial for manufacturing nanodevices. "Given the size scale, no other approach appears to be practical," Yurke said. "This may lead to a test-tube based nanofabrication technology that assembles complex structures, such as electronic circuits, through the orderly addition of molecules." 

While DNA typically exists in a double-stranded form - similar to a twisted ladder -- the researchers began with three single strands, each resembling a ladder sliced down the middle. Strand A has the correct DNA sequence to latch onto half of strand B and half of strand C, and so joins them all together. Strand A also has a hinge section between the parts that bind to B and C, so that the two "arms" -- AB and AC -- can move freely. 

On its own, the DNA structure floats with its arms wide open. The arms are pulled shut by adding a DNA fuel strand, which is designed to attach to the dangling, unpaired sections of strands B and C. To re-open the tweezers, the fuel strand is removed by adding another strand with the right DNA sequence to pair up with it. 

"The entire population of 30 trillion DNA tweezers in a few drops of solution can be repeatedly closed and opened by successively adding fuel and removal strands," said Andrew Turberfield, a physicist at the University of Oxford, who spent a recent sabbatical year at Bell Labs. Other scientists participating in the research were physicist Allen Mills and post-doctoral fellow Friedrich Simmel of Bell Labs and Jennifer Neumann, a graduate student at Rutgers University. 

Because the DNA motors are too small to be observed with available microscopic techniques, the researchers relied on the phenomenon of fluorescence to detect the closing and opening actions. A pair of dye molecules was attached to the ends of the DNA motors, and when laser light "excited" the dyes, the amount of fluorescent light indicated the distance between the two ends. 

Yurke said he was inspired to devise DNA motors when he realized molecular-scale protein motors in living organisms are responsible for muscular contraction and moving substances around in cells. 

The Bell Labs scientists are already working to attach DNA to electrically conducting molecules to assemble rudimentary molecular-scale electronic circuits. 

Bell Labs is celebrating its 75th anniversary this year. One of the most innovative R&D entities in the world, Bell Labs has generated more than 40,000 inventions since 1925. It has played a pivotal role in inventing or perfecting key communications technologies for most of the 20th century, including transistors, digital networking and signal processing, lasers and fiber-optic communications systems, communications satellites, cellular telephony, electronic switching of calls, touch-tone dialing, and modems. 

Today, Bell Labs continues to draw some of the best scientific minds. With more than 30,000 employees located in 25 countries, it is the largest R&D organization in the world dedicated to communications and the world's leading source of new communications technologies. In a recent report, Technology Review magazine said Bell Labs patents had the greatest impact on telecommunications for 1999. 

Lucent Technologies, headquartered in Murray Hill, N.J., U.S.A., designs and delivers the systems, software, silicon and services for next-generation communications networks for service providers and enterprises. Backed by the research and development of Bell Labs, Lucent focuses on high-growth areas such as optical and wireless networks; Internet infrastructure; communications software; communications semiconductors and optoelectronics; Web-based enterprise solutions that link private and public networks; and professional network design and consulting services. For more information on Lucent Technologies and Bell Labs, visit the company's Web site at http://www.lucent.com or the Bell Labs Web site at http://www.bell-labs.com.

AUSTIN, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sept. 15, 2000--Convergent Investors, LLC, a Texas-based venture capital investment group, has closed a $64 million venture capital fund. 

The establishment of Convergent Investors VI, LP, represents the latest phase in the investment activities of a group of successful local entrepreneurs who have co-invested in technology-based deals over the last two years. 

Prior to the establishment of the fund, members of the Convergent Investors group have invested in 11 early-stage companies, primarily in Texas. The new fund will be invested in early-stage high technology, telecommunications, e-commerce and transaction-oriented businesses. Favored companies will serve rapidly growing and large-scale markets or develop new technologies which are far reaching in scope and potential market size. The majority of the fund is expected to be invested within three years. 

Prior Convergent group investments include six Austin-based start-up companies: Broadjump Inc., Netpliance Inc. (Nasdaq:NPLI), Chicory Systems Inc., Grande Communications Inc., Nanoscale Engineering and Technology Group Inc. and Zebra Imaging Inc. Additional investments include GT Group Telecom (Nasdaq:GTTLB), a leading Canadian telecommunications company now headquartered in Toronto. 

Convergent Investors, LLC, has offices in Austin and Houston. The Austin-based general partners are Jimmy Mansour, Brian Smith and Willard Hanzlik; the Houston-based general partners are John Chaney, Robert Gauntt and Steve Shaper. A seventh general partner, Henry James, is based in Seattle. The general partners bring a wealth of experience in private investing and in building technology-based enterprises. 

Jimmy Mansour is the founder of two independent telecommunications companies and is nationally recognized as a leader in the communications industry; Brian Smith is the co-founder and CEO of Crossroads Systems Inc. (Nasdaq:CRDS). Willard Hanzlik is an active private investor and former principal of The Sterling Group, a Houston-based leveraged buyout firm. John Chaney and Steve Shaper were founders and chief executive officers of Telecheck Inc., a national transaction services business now owned by First Data Corporation. Robert Gauntt is a principal in the private wealth management group of Morgan Stanley & Co. Henry James is a former general partner of Goldman Sachs & Co, with responsibility for the firm's operations in Japan. 

For more information on Convergent Investors VI, LP, their partners and investments, please consult the Web at www.convergentinvestors.com.

Orange County Water District's Water Resources and Technology Team Offers Online Services 

813 words 
19 September 2000
21:58 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(Copyright (c) 2000, Business Wire) 

FOUNTAIN VALLEY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sept. 19, 2000-- 

Web Site Offers a Wealth of Useful Technical Information to 

Prospective Clients and New Research Partners 

Orange County Water District's (OCWD) Water Resources & Technology Department recently completed development of a technical Web site which provides detailed descriptions of membrane analytical services that are now offered to prospective clients and new research partners. 

The Web site can be found at www.MicroMemAnalytical.com. 

The membrane-research Web site was developed by a new enterprise division at OCWD -- comprised of members of OCWD's membrane-research team -- to provide prospective clients and new research partners with information on OCWD's research capabilities and services. 

Over the past several years, the research team has developed unique methodologies for observing and manipulating membrane surfaces on a sub-micron scale. They have designed special microscope flow cells (MFCs) that can be used to quickly screen for and evaluate which types of chemical treatments and formulations prevent membrane surfaces from undergoing fouling. 

The MFCs are essentially miniature reverse osmosis membrane systems with microscope viewing ports. This kind of micro-technology facilitates and shortens the time required to search for and validate new membrane cleaning agents that can be used to lower the operational and energy costs associated with modern membrane systems -- the future of water purification. 

OCWD's research team offers membrane surface characterization, performance testing, cleaning chemical and biocide screening and microbial identification using modern molecular (i.e., DNA-based) techniques. 

For example, clients are offered quick turnaround, computer-assisted design of polymerase chain reaction (PCR)(1) primers and probe sequences for the rapid detection of bacterial pathogens that cause various plant, animal and human diseases. Molecular identification of bacteria is an extremely important and rapidly evolving area of research in the water, agricultural, environmental and public-health sectors of the global economy. 

"We offer full-service PCR primer and probe design, which allows us to provide everything from initial specific primer(2) identification to final sequencing and identification to strain level," said Dr. Harry Ridgway, director of research at OCWD. 

Using such molecular methods, it is now possible to rapidly and inexpensively characterize entire communities of bacteria in environmental samples, including soil, air, water and even membrane biofilms. 

"Accurate microbial characterization of membrane biofilms is an extremely important capability if we want to understand just how certain microbes impact the performance, efficiency and safety of membrane facilities around the world," said Ridgway. 

Membrane-related services offered by www.MicroMemAnalytical.com and the OCWD membrane-research team include rapid and inexpensive lab tests that measure and compare the biofouling potentials of new and existing water treatment membranes; characterization and analysis of the surface topography of membranes by atomic force microscopy and other techniques; molecular modeling of membrane polymer structure and function; and bench-scale membrane performance testing and analysis. 

Besides membranes, the research team also offers molecular-modeling services for other kinds of systems, such as modeling of bacterial polymers that are involved in stabilizing membrane biofilms, or modeling of disinfection byproduct formation reaction mechanisms. 

OCWD's research team's capabilities are used by clients not only to improve polymer membrane performance, but also to investigate diffusion and surface fouling mechanisms. 

"We are excited about this new Web site and plan to use it extensively as a technology transfer vehicle for communicating our research capabilities and findings to water agencies, funding organizations, new clients, research partners and other interested parties," said Ridgway. 

Questions or comments about www.MicroMemAnalytical.com should be directed to: Dr. Harry Ridgway, Research Director, Water Resources & Technology, Orange County Water District, 10500 Ellis Ave., Fountain Valley, Calif. 92708. Ridgway may also be reached by phone at 714/378-3266 or by e-mail at hridgway@ocwd.com. 

Orange County Water District is a special agency that was created by the California State Legislature in 1933 to maintain and manage the groundwater basin under northern and central Orange County. 

OCWD's groundwater basin supplies 75 percent of the water needs in Anaheim, Buena Park, Costa Mesa, Cypress, Fountain Valley, Fullerton, Garden Grove, Huntington Beach, Irvine, La Palma, Los Alamitos, Newport Beach, Orange, Placentia, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, Stanton, Tustin, Villa Park, Westminster and Yorba Linda. 

(1) PCR (polymerase chain reaction) is a molecular method in which specific DNA sequences are amplified for the purpose of detecting and identifying microorganisms. Using PCR makes it possible to amplify a gene more than a million fold; a single bacterial cell can be detected by PCR. 

(2) A short piece of DNA added to one end of a strand of DNA in order to define the portion to be copied.

Speaker David Bodanis offers these sample predictions: 

Neurobiology in 2020: 

History indicates that a human's mental agility begins to deteriorate by the age of 40. Researchers in the mid 20th century realised that much of this was due to the decay of a small cluster of cells in the hippocampus - the region of the brain which turns short-term memory into long-term data storage. By 2020, advances in stem cell technology will have eradicated that problem. HR therapy (Hippocampal Rejuvenation therapy) will ensure that individuals of any age can retain the same ability to process and remember thoughts, ideas and sensations at the same capacities they had in their youth. Unfortunately, the great cost of this therapy will mean that a two-tier society will develop around the world. The wealthy will be able to afford it; the majority will not. 

Transport in 2020: 

The fuel cell will be refined to a level only imagined in the advanced laboratories at the start of the 21st century. It will be common in 2020 for parents, at the end of a long car drive, to sit their children down by the side of the road and have them drink from the car's exhaust pipe. As the parent floors the accelerator to rev the engine, a healthy refreshing supply of crystal-clear cool water will gush out. In many developed countries this will be regarded merely as a handy convenience, but in hotter or land-locked parts of the world, cars and trucks will be seen as wondrous sources of life-giving water. In 2020, it will be difficult to comprehend that vehicles were once criticised as mobile pollution sources or that people once paid a premium for housing that guaranteed they'd live far from road fumes.

Packard Foundation Awards $15 Million to Promising Young Scientific Researchers; 2000 Packard Fellowships in Science and Engineering 

1,379 words 
25 October 2000
12:08 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(Copyright (c) 2000, Business Wire) 

LOS ALTOS, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 25, 2000--Twenty-four of the most promising science and engineering researchers at 22 universities across the United States have been awarded five-year fellowships worth $625,000 each from the David and Lucile Packard Foundation. 

Now in its thirteenth year, the Packard Fellowships Program provides 24 new faculty members with $125,000 per year over five years to support their scientific research. It is one of the nation's largest non-governmental programs of unrestricted grants to young university faculty in science and engineering. From the study of galaxies, the earth, and its atmosphere, to cell biology, to nanotechnology and materials design, to theoretical mathematics and physics, the Fellows' research covers a multitude of disciplines in science and engineering. 

"The unrestricted nature of the fellowship, along with the commitment of funding for five years, will enable the Fellows to pursue lines of inquiry that might be too risky for standard funding mechanisms," said Lynn Orr, dean of earth sciences at Stanford University and chairman of the advisory panel that selects fellowship recipients. "This approach reflects David Packard's style of operation: find talented people and give them the resources they need to do top quality work, along with the responsibility to determine how best to use those resources." 

Since 1988, the Foundation has awarded fellowships totaling $155 million to 272 faculty members at 50 universities in the United States. The fellowships were established to develop future scientific leaders, to further the work of promising young scientists and engineers, to encourage networking among these researchers, and to support efforts to attract talented graduate students into university research in the United States. 

"This new group of Packard Fellows represents an investment in talented young faculty," added Orr. "Their research will benefit society in the decades to come, and the students who work with them will make contributions that will multiply the value of the research effort many times over." 

The 2000 Fellows were nominated by their university presidents and recommended by a panel of nationally recognized scientists and engineers. Fellows were selected this year from universities in the following states: California, Connecticut, Georgia, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Washington. 

The David and Lucile Packard Foundation is a private family foundation created in 1964 by David Packard (1912-1996), co-founder of the Hewlett-Packard Company and Lucile Salter Packard (1914-1987). The Foundation provides grants to nonprofit organizations in the following broad program areas: conservation; population; science; children, families, and communities; arts; and organizational effectiveness and philanthropy. The Foundation makes grants at the national and international level, and also has a special focus on the Northern California counties of San Mateo, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, and Monterey. The Foundation's assets were approxi-mately $14 billion as of July 31, 2000. Grant awards totaled approximately $411 million in 1999, and the Foundation expects to make grants of approximately $500 million in 2000.

NanoWorld Projects Announces Launch of New Expansion Company in Europe 

380 words 
26 October 2000
13:26 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(Copyright (c) 2000, Business Wire) 

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 26, 2000--NanoWorld Projects' (OTCBB:NAPH) (Website: www.nanoworldprojects.com) Chairman, Robert Papalia, today announced the official opening of NanoWorld's European subsidiary, NanoWorld International in Turin, Italy. 

The new company has been formed in recognition of the strength of international interest in NanoWorld's technology and in order to work more closely with key strategic partners located in Europe. 

"This is a very exciting move for us," said Papalia. "We will now have a European office focusing on sales, marketing, and development for our nanotechnology initiative. With this new company in action, our research center in Turin will be able to dedicate itself exclusively to nanotechnology research and development, for faster expansion of this extraordinary technology." 

Nanotechnology is a revolutionary new field involving engineering at the molecular level. NanoWorld's technology has the potential to transform many current manufacturing processes in a wide range of product areas such as super-conductors, data storage, filtration systems, bio-medical sensors, and fiber optics. 

"Our patented Dynamic Thin Laminar Flow (DTLF) process enables the production of single- or multi-layer films for various applications," said Giorgio Marioni, NanoWorld President. "We continue to strive to be a leader in the nanotechnology field. With offices located in New York, British Columbia, Quebec, and Europe, we now have a true global presence to raise the profile and advance the development of nanotechnology". 

About NanoWorld Projects Corporation 

NanoWorld Projects is pioneering the industrialization of a revolutionary new field of building materials at the molecular level. The company expects its nanotechnology applications to facilitate great technological strides in many disciplines including health, chemistry, electricity, and optics. Nanotechnology can potentially affect a wide range of manufacturing processes from the creation of computer chips with greater storage and processing capabilities to highly effective anti-corrosion coatings for shipbuilding.

Veeco Reports 2000 Third Quarter and Nine Month Results 

2,317 words 
27 October 2000
00:07 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(Copyright (c) 2000, Business Wire) 

PLAINVIEW, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 26, 2000--Veeco Instruments Inc. (NASDAQ: VECO) today announced its financial results for the third quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2000. Historical results have been restated to include the merger with CVC, Inc., which closed on May 5, 2000 and was accounted for as a pooling of interests. Veeco pre-announced third quarter results on October 5th. 

Third Quarter Results 

Veeco's sales for the third quarter of 2000 were $92.9 million, a 7% increase over the $87.0 million reported in the third quarter of 1999. As previously announced, while Veeco's sales were up versus the prior year period, these results were disappointing when compared to previous third quarter 2000 sales forecasts of $104 million. Lower sales were principally the result of a $7 million sales shortfall at Veeco's recently acquired CVC subsidiary, due to delayed orders and shipments from data storage and specialty semiconductor customers, which caused a $0.15 reduction in earnings per share for the third quarter versus prior guidance. Veeco's Ion Tech subsidiary, currently increasing production in response to significant demand for its SPECTOR(TM) IBD system, increased its revenue 50% over the prior quarter, despite delayed shipments in the last weeks of the quarter. These delays were due primarily to longer customer acceptance test times associated with the addition of a newly developed in-situ, automated optical measurement system (OMS). The missed shipments at Ion Tech resulted in a $0.05 earnings per share miss in the third quarter versus prior forecasts. Veeco's Process Equipment sales were $47.5 million, an 8% decrease from the $51.8 million reported in the third quarter of last year. Third quarter Metrology sales were a record $42.8 million, a 38% increase over the $31.2 million reported in the third quarter of 1999, driven primarily by sales of atomic force microscopes to semiconductor customers. 

Bookings for the third quarter of 2000 were a record $179.9 million, a 106% increase over the $87.2 million in the third quarter of 1999, and up 36% sequentially over the second quarter of 2000. Approximately half of Veeco's third quarter bookings were from optical telecommunications customers. Veeco's Process Equipment bookings were $125.4 million, a 122% increase over the $56.4 million in the third quarter of 1999. Veeco's Ion Tech subsidiary, which manufactures ion beam deposition systems used to manufacture Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) filters, reported a 1,085% increase in third quarter bookings to $85.3 million from $7.2 million in the prior year third quarter. Process Equipment bookings (excluding Ion Tech) decreased 18% to $40.1 million from $49.2 million in the prior year third quarter. 

Veeco's third quarter Metrology bookings increased 92% to $52.1 million from the $27.2 million in the third quarter of 1999, including an 82% increase in atomic force microscopes and a 118% increase in optical metrology products. Veeco's family of automated semiconductor metrology tools (Vx Atomic Force Profiler and the Dimension 9000 Atomic Force Microscope) reported record third quarter orders due to their recent adoption by leading semiconductor manufacturers. Veeco's third quarter book/bill ratio was 1.94. 

Veeco's third quarter 2000 operating income was $7.4 million compared with $11.2 million (excluding non-recurring charges of $1.2 million) in the third quarter of 1999, a decrease of 35%. Net income was $6.1 million in the third quarter of 2000 versus $6.2 million in the corresponding period of last year. Diluted earnings per share for the third quarter of 2000 were $0.24 per share compared to $0.29 per share in the third quarter of 1999. Third quarter 1999 pro forma diluted earnings per share were $0.32 when calculated on a fully taxed basis, excluding a $1.2 million charge to earnings incurred by CVC in relation to their Commonwealth Scientific acquisition. Pro forma diluted earnings per share for the third quarter was $0.20, which is calculated using a fully taxed rate and which excludes non-deductible charges related to the mergers with CVC and Monarch Labs. As previously announced, earnings per share were below Veeco's prior guidance of between $0.38 - $0.42 per share, principally the result of Veeco's recently acquired CVC division's $7.0 million sales shortfall and a $5.0 million shortfall at Ion Tech. 

Nine Month Results 

Veeco's sales for the first nine months of 2000 were a record $264.4 million, an 11% increase over the $238.6 million for the first nine months of 1999. Process Equipment nine month sales increased slightly to $139.4 million, compared to $137.2 million in the first nine months of last year. Nine month 2000 Metrology sales were a record $116.9 million, a 33% increase over the $87.6 million in the first nine months of 1999. 

Veeco's first nine month 2000 bookings were a record $423.6 million, a 62% increase over the $261.3 million in the first nine months of 1999. Process Equipment nine month bookings were a record $269.6 million, a 56% increase over the $173.0 million reported in the first nine months of 1999. Metrology bookings for the first nine months of 2000 were a record $145.7 million, an increase of 88% from the $77.5 million last year. Veeco's nine-month book/bill ratio was 1.6. 

In the first nine months of 2000, Veeco's operating income was $18.8 million (excluding previously reported non-recurring charges of $33.3 million principally related to the merger with CVC) compared to $33.2 million (excluding $1.2 million in non-recurring charges) in the first nine months of 1999, a decline of 44%. Net income in the first nine months of 2000 was $12.8 million (excluding non-recurring charges) compared to $20.8 million last year (excluding non-recurring charges), a decline of 39%. Including non-recurring charges, Veeco reported a net loss of $6.6 million in the first nine months of 2000. Excluding non-recurring charges, pro forma diluted earnings per share in the first nine months of 2000 was $0.51 per share compared to $0.98 per share last year. Veeco's decline in profitability in 2000 versus the prior year is primarily attributable to the lower gross margins experienced in the Company's data storage Process Equipment businesses. 

Management Review of Results 

Regarding these results, Edward H. Braun, Veeco's Chairman and CEO commented, "Despite strong market demand reflected by record order activity, quarterly shipments from CVC and Ion Tech divisions were disappointing. Corrective actions have been taken to assure sales and profit growth for the fourth quarter and 2001. Looking ahead, we are optimistic about the prospects for Veeco's growth based upon our strong bookings of optical telecommunication equipment and metrology products, as well as continued strength in semiconductor products." 

Mr. Braun continued, "As we stated several weeks ago, we have revised our revenue and earnings growth forecasts for the fourth quarter of 2000 and for 2001 to reflect a more moderate sales and profit ramp going forward. We are currently forecasting that fourth quarter 2000 sales will be approximately $110 million, with earnings in the range of $0.32 - $0.37 per share. For 2001, we are forecasting revenues of approximately $570 million with forecasted earnings per share in the range of $2.40 to $2.50 per share. These revised forecasts are supported by a record backlog and strong customer acceptance of our products. Demand for our products is very strong: our order rate for the last six month period is now running at an annualized rate of $600 million per year. Our focus going forward will be on improved operational execution at CVC and Ion Tech." 

Investor Information 

Veeco is hosting an investor conference call at 10:00am ET tomorrow, Friday, October 27th, to review the Company's financials and operations for the third quarter and nine month periods. 

The call will be open to all interested parties through a live audio web broadcast via the Internet at http://www.veeco.com(click on Investor Information). This call will be archived for future reference. A telephonic playback of the conference call will also be available from 1:00pm EST on Friday, October 27th through 5:00pm EST on Friday, November 3rd. Listeners should call 888-203-1112 and use Reservation number 401799. 

Veeco is also hosting an analyst meeting in New York on Tuesday, October 31st at 12:00 pm ET. Management's presentation at this meeting will be broadcast live (beginning at approximately 12:30pm) on the internet at the Veeco website, listed above. 

About Veeco 

Veeco Instruments Inc. is a worldwide leader in process equipment and metrology tools for the optical telecommunications, data storage, semiconductor and research markets. Manufacturing and engineering facilities are located in New York, California, Colorado, Arizona and Minnesota. Global sales and service offices are located throughout the United States, Europe, Japan and Asia Pacific. Additional information on Veeco can be found at http://www.veeco.com. 

To the extent that this news release discusses expectations about market conditions or about market acceptance and future sales of Veeco's products, or otherwise makes statements about the future, such statements are forward-looking and are subject to a number of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from the statements made. These factors include the cyclical nature of the data storage, optical telecommunications and semiconductor industries, risks associated with the acceptance of new products by individual customers and by the marketplace, and other factors discussed in the Business Description and Management's Discussion and Analysis sections of Veeco's Report on Form 10-K and Annual Report to Shareholders.

NanoGram Concludes $25 Million Funding

31 October 2000
14:02 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(Copyright (c) 2000, Business Wire) 

FREMONT, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 31, 2000--NanoGram Corporation, a world leader in the synthesis of complex compounds and the manufacture of nano-material based products, today announced completion of a $25 million round of financing. This represents the final phase of this round of funding for the company. 

NanoGram has developed core process technology enabling the manufacture of unique nanoscale compositions. This process technology has successfully been exploited in the manufacture of energy storage, optical and electronic materials, applications and systems. 

Corporate investors Dow Corning of the U.S., NEC Corporation of Japan and ABB of Zurich, Switzerland were joined by several new venture investors. Bay Partners, a firm active in early stage fundamental technology investing, was joined by Hydro Quebec CapiTech of Canada, France's Groupe Siparex, Japan's Techno-Venture, SBV Venture Partners, Fountainhead Capital, XR Ventures and Sands Brothers in completing the round. Continuing investors included Institutional Venture Partners, Venrock Associates and Nth Power Technologies. 

Nanotechnology is the creation and utilization of functional materials, devices and systems with novel properties that are achieved through the control of matter at the molecular level. Nanoscale materials are those that are intermediate between isolated atoms and bulk materials. Nanotechnology is enabling revolutions in areas as diverse as catalysts, energy and life sciences. 

NanoGram's in-place, patented production techniques allow the Company to develop and produce chemically diverse compounds, many of which do not occur in nature. The Company's laser-based manufacturing technology produces nanoparticles, materials and products for a variety of novel applications. The pace of discovery in nanotechnology is greatly accelerating. 

Optical coatings and components are produced using NanoGram's patented laser-driven process technology. The company has developed and patented Laser Reactive Deposition technology (LRD(TM)) for unique nanoscale compositions that enables high throughput, low cost production of wafer-based passive and active optical components. NanoGram's nanoparticle manufacturing system (NPM(TM)) allows volume production of the most complex and highest value nanoscale materials and structures available. 

"Nanomaterials are emerging as important building blocks for advancing materials technology used in high-performance optical and electronic devices," explained Tim Jenks, the firm's CEO. "NanoGram expects to continue its optical and electronic development activities and will add pilot level production for optical materials and components within six months," he continued. 

Hal Stillman, Vice President of Technology at ABB Inc. said, "ABB, Inc. has an active international research and development agenda in nanotechnology. NanoGram's processes deliver unique nano-crystalline materials that may have applications in various aspects of ABB's business activities. This investment underlines ABB's interest in exploring potential applications of nanomaterials with NanoGram." 

NanoGram is a privately held corporation with world headquarters in Fremont, Calif., USA.

Targeted Molecules Corp. Founded by a Leading Scientist From the Burnham Institute 

923 words 
31 October 2000
18:50 GMT
Business Wire 
English
(Copyright (c) 2000, Business Wire) 

LA JOLLA, Calif.--(BW HealthWire)--Oct. 31, 2000-- 

New Company to Establish Leadership Position in Developing Molecular 

Map of the Vasculature Through in Vivo Phage Peptide Display 

Targeted Molecules Corp. ("TMC"), an emerging biotechnology company, announced today that it will use its proprietary technologies to develop an extensive molecular map of the mouse and human vasculature. 

The company's unique technology platform uses in vivo screening of phage combinatorial libraries to identify peptides that home selectively to specific tissues or disease sites. This broadly enabling technology was originally developed at The Burnham Institute, La Jolla. It has revealed a surprising degree of specialization in the vasculature of individual tissues, healthy or diseased. A large library of proprietary vascular homing peptides has already been generated. Some of these peptides home to the vasculature of specific tissues or organs, irrespective of whether the tissue is healthy or diseased, whereas other peptides home only to certain diseased tissues, such as tumors or inflammatory sites. 

"This type of molecular signature in the vasculature of healthy or disease tissue is unprecedented. It offers a new avenue to drug discovery by the use of these peptides as lead molecules to identify their receptors. Furthermore they can be used to target various molecular entities and concentrate them to their desired vascular site of action, thus minimizing undesired side effects," commented Dr. Elias Lazarides, president and chief executive officer. "The opportunity afforded to TMC is to develop a comprehensive library of peptides, the receptors they bind to and the potential ligands they may mimic. By combining the in vivo screening data with extensive histological analysis of mouse and human tissues we can provide a detailed molecular map of the vasculature of any organ, healthy or diseased. This is a major bioinformatics undertaking for the company. We expect to isolate and map the binding sites for thousands of peptides. We refer to this novel approach as `Angiomics.' This proprietary approach will provide specific targeting vehicles for drugs, particles, gene therapy vectors, cells, nanodevices, growth factors, cytokines or in general for diagnostic purposes. In addition, once the receptors have been identified the peptides will provide lead molecules for drug discovery. The angiomics approach will draw from the emerging genomics information and complement it." 

TMC's founder, Dr. Erkki Ruoslahti, president and chief executive officer of The Burnham Institute and chairman of the board of TMC, is a leading authority in cell adhesion. He was one of the discoverers of fibronectin, identified several of the prototypic integrins, and discovered that a small tripeptide is responsible for the recognition of fibronectin and many other adhesion proteins. Most recently, he devised the in vivo phage display method that his laboratory has used to show the molecular specialization of the vasculature that is the basis of TMC's technology. Ruoslahti and coworkers have generated the initial set of proprietary targeting peptides licensed to the company. They have isolated peptides targeting the vasculature of a large number of organs and tissues as well as peptides that specifically target the neovasculature of tumors, and angiogenic sites of other diseases. The therapeutic benefit gained by coupling a cytotoxic anticancer drug linked to a tumor neovascular homing peptide has been demonstrated in targeting models of cancer in his laboratory. Furthermore, the power of this technology for the identification of novel receptors for drug discovery has been substantiated by the identification of aminopeptidase N as the receptor for a peptide that homes to tumor vasculature. 

A special application of this technology has been the development of a proprietary method for non-surgical organ and tissue ablation at The Burnham Institute. Peptides capable of inducing apoptosis by disrupting the mitochondrial membranes in target cells can induce tissue specific shrinkage when coupled to homing peptides. Proof-of-concept for this principle for neovascular therapeutic targets has already been obtained in mouse experimental models by linking the proapoptotic peptides to the appropriate angiogenic homing peptide. 

The Burnham Institute is a founding shareholder of TMC. The Institute engaged Dr. Elias Lazarides to co-found and lead the new company. Dr. Lazarides brings with him a wealth of experience both in academia and in the pharmaceutical industry. Most recently he was president of Tanabe Research Laboratories in San Diego. Prior to that he served as the president and chief operation officer of a subsidiary of Alliance Pharmaceutical Corp. He joined the pharmaceutical industry as executive director of Research at Merck & Co. after 15 years as a Professor of Biology at the California Institute of Technology. 

TMC has already assembled a distinguished Board of Directors whose members, in addition to Drs. Ruoslahti and Lazarides, include Dr. Blake Ingle, managing partner of IngleWood Ventures, and past president and chief executive officer of Canji Inc., and chairman of the board of The Burnham Institute; Thomas A. Page, who was for many years the chairman, president and chief executive officer of San Diego Gas and Electric (now Sempra Energy); and Vickie L. Capps, CPA, currently vice president, Finance and Administration, chief financial officer and treasurer of Maxwell Technologies Inc. Information on the financing and corporate alliances of TMC will be forthcoming.

The Science of Very Small Things is Making Big Waves

ANN ARBOR, Mich.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 6, 2000-- 

Dr. Kensall D. Wise of the University of Michigan College 

of Engineering offers expertise and insight into one of 

today's hottest science topics: nanotechnology

Dr. Kensall D. Wise, an authority on the scientific complexities and foreseeable benefits of nanotechnologies, is now welcoming queries from the media in an effort to promote educated public debate. Nanotechnology has become one of today's hottest topics, thanks in part to President Clinton's January announcement of the National Nanotechnology Initiative, a $227 million increase in the government's investment in R&D on the manipulation of individual atoms to build mechanical and information machines on a nanometer scale. 

Professor Wise is the Director of the University of Michigan Engineering Research Center (ERC) on Wireless Integrated Microsystems (WIMS). He is currently overseeing two significant research testbeds, one focused on implantable neural protheses and a second on large scale environmental monitoring. He can provide realistic and substantive insights about the social and economic potential of this new science. Professor Wise has worked for over thirty years on microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), particularly on sensor-circuit integration and microsystems. He is a member of the National Academy of Engineering and is internationally recognized as a leader in MEMS technology. 

In September 2000, The National Science Foundation announced the establishment of the nation's first Engineering Research Center for WIMS at the University of Michigan College of Engineering. This designation will result in more than $60 million in funding to further explore and develop the potential benefits of WIMS. This ERC is the country's premier research center on wireless nanotechnologies, with first-year funding from the NSF of $2.5 million and an additional $2+ million in contributions from the State of Michigan, partnering universities, and a consortium of global industry including General Motors, Ford, Intel and Texas Instruments. 

Relevant Commentary 

What might these things do? They will probably be sent into human bodies to find cancer, then make and deliver cancer-fighting drugs on the spot. They might be the atomic-scale chips and memory of next-generation computers thousands of times more powerful that those that run on silicon technology. They could be molded into the material of tires - millions of tiny pressure gauges and pumps capable of knowing the air pressure inside and keeping the tire inflated. . . . Though it may take a decade or two, nanotech will become a huge area of invention and commerce." Kevin Maney, "No Need to Fear: Nanotechnology Is Near," USA Today, October 24, 2000. 

Nanoscience is [Newt] Gingrich's favorite subject. . . . `I believe that we're actually at the edge of an age of discovery which is vastly richer than anyone understands,' he said...The change, he said, might be so great that the expression "orders of magnitude" would be too modest to express it. James Traub, "Newt at Rest," The New York Times Magazine, October 29,2000.
